O(n log k) 
import java.util.*;

public class HeapsTopK {

    // ---------- Kth Largest: keep a MIN-heap of size k (LC 215) ----------
    // RECOGNIZE: "k largest / smallest / most frequent / closest". Heap of size k -> O(n log k).
    static int findKthLargest(int[] a, int k) {
        PriorityQueue<Integer> pq = new PriorityQueue<>();
        for (int x : a) { pq.add(x); if (pq.size() > k) pq.poll(); }
        return pq.peek();
    }

    // Quickselect: average O(n), worst O(n^2) -- randomize the pivot
    static int quickselectKthLargest(int[] a, int k) {
        int[] b = a.clone();
        int target = b.length - k, lo = 0, hi = b.length - 1;
        Random rnd = new Random(1);
        while (lo < hi) {
            int p = b[lo + rnd.nextInt(hi - lo + 1)], i = lo, j = hi;
            while (i <= j) { // Hoare-style three-way-safe partition
                while (b[i] < p) i++;
                while (b[j] > p) j--;
                if (i <= j) { int t = b[i]; b[i] = b[j]; b[j] = t; i++; j--; }
            }
            if (target <= j) hi = j; else if (target >= i) lo = i; else return b[target];
        }
        return b[target];
    }

    // K Closest Points to Origin (LC 973): MAX-heap of size k on distance
    static int[][] kClosest(int[][] pts, int k) {
        PriorityQueue<int[]> pq = new PriorityQueue<>((a, b) -> Long.compare(d2(b), d2(a)));
        for (int[] p : pts) { pq.add(p); if (pq.size() > k) pq.poll(); }
        return pq.toArray(new int[0][]);
    }

    private static long d2(int[] p) { return (long) p[0] * p[0] + (long) p[1] * p[1]; }

    // Top K Frequent Words (LC 692): tie-break alphabetical
    static List<String> topKFrequentWords(String[] words, int k) {
        Map<String, Integer> f = new HashMap<>();
        for (String w : words) f.merge(w, 1, Integer::sum);
        PriorityQueue<String> pq = new PriorityQueue<>((a, b) -> f.get(a).equals(f.get(b)) ? b.compareTo(a) : f.get(a) - f.get(b));
        for (String w : f.keySet()) { pq.add(w); if (pq.size() > k) pq.poll(); }
        LinkedList<String> res = new LinkedList<>();
        while (!pq.isEmpty()) res.addFirst(pq.poll());
        return res;
    }

    // ---------- Two heaps: Find Median from Data Stream (LC 295) ----------
    static class MedianFinder {
        private final PriorityQueue<Integer> lo = new PriorityQueue<>(Collections.reverseOrder()); // lower half
        private final PriorityQueue<Integer> hi = new PriorityQueue<>();                           // upper half
        void addNum(int x) {
            lo.add(x);
            hi.add(lo.poll());
            if (hi.size() > lo.size()) lo.add(hi.poll());
        }
        double findMedian() { return lo.size() > hi.size() ? lo.peek() : (lo.peek() + (double) hi.peek()) / 2; }
    }

    // Sliding Window Median (LC 480): TreeMap-free version with two multiset heaps + lazy delete is long;
    // this simple O(n k) insertion version is the safe interview baseline.
    static double[] medianSlidingWindow(int[] a, int k) {
        double[] res = new double[a.length - k + 1];
        List<Integer> win = new ArrayList<>();
        for (int i = 0; i < a.length; i++) {
            int pos = Collections.binarySearch(win, a[i]);
            win.add(pos < 0 ? -pos - 1 : pos, a[i]);
            if (i >= k) win.remove(Collections.binarySearch(win, a[i - k]));
            if (i >= k - 1)
                res[i - k + 1] = k % 2 == 1 ? win.get(k / 2) : ((long) win.get(k / 2 - 1) + win.get(k / 2)) / 2.0;
        }
        return res;
    }

    // ---------- Merge K sorted lists / arrays (LC 23): heap of (value, list, index) ----------
    static List<Integer> mergeKSorted(List<int[]> lists) {
        PriorityQueue<int[]> pq = new PriorityQueue<>((x, y) -> x[0] - y[0]); // {value, listIdx, elemIdx}
        for (int i = 0; i < lists.size(); i++) if (lists.get(i).length > 0) pq.add(new int[]{lists.get(i)[0], i, 0});
        List<Integer> out = new ArrayList<>();
        while (!pq.isEmpty()) {
            int[] t = pq.poll();
            out.add(t[0]);
            int[] src = lists.get(t[1]);
            if (t[2] + 1 < src.length) pq.add(new int[]{src[t[2] + 1], t[1], t[2] + 1});
        }
        return out;
    }

    // Kth Smallest in Sorted Matrix (LC 378)
    static int kthSmallest(int[][] m, int k) {
        int n = m.length;
        PriorityQueue<int[]> pq = new PriorityQueue<>((a, b) -> a[0] - b[0]);
        for (int i = 0; i < Math.min(n, k); i++) pq.add(new int[]{m[i][0], i, 0});
        int v = 0;
        while (k-- > 0) {
            int[] t = pq.poll();
            v = t[0];
            if (t[2] + 1 < n) pq.add(new int[]{m[t[1]][t[2] + 1], t[1], t[2] + 1});
        }
        return v;
    }

    // Smallest Range Covering Elements from K Lists (LC 632)
    static int[] smallestRange(List<List<Integer>> nums) {
        PriorityQueue<int[]> pq = new PriorityQueue<>((a, b) -> a[0] - b[0]);
        int max = Integer.MIN_VALUE;
        for (int i = 0; i < nums.size(); i++) { pq.add(new int[]{nums.get(i).get(0), i, 0}); max = Math.max(max, nums.get(i).get(0)); }
        int[] best = {pq.peek()[0], max};
        while (true) {
            int[] t = pq.poll();
            if (max - t[0] < best[1] - best[0]) best = new int[]{t[0], max};
            if (t[2] + 1 == nums.get(t[1]).size()) break;
            int nv = nums.get(t[1]).get(t[2] + 1);
            max = Math.max(max, nv);
            pq.add(new int[]{nv, t[1], t[2] + 1});
        }
        return best;
    }

    // ---------- Greedy with heap ----------
    // Task Scheduler (LC 621): closed form
    static int leastInterval(char[] tasks, int n) {
        int[] c = new int[26];
        int max = 0, maxCount = 0;
        for (char t : tasks) max = Math.max(max, ++c[t - 'A']);
        for (int x : c) if (x == max) maxCount++;
        return Math.max(tasks.length, (max - 1) * (n + 1) + maxCount);
    }

    // Reorganize String (LC 767): always place the most frequent char that is not the previous one
    static String reorganizeString(String s) {
        int[] c = new int[26];
        for (char ch : s.toCharArray()) c[ch - 'a']++;
        PriorityQueue<int[]> pq = new PriorityQueue<>((a, b) -> b[1] - a[1]);
        for (int i = 0; i < 26; i++) if (c[i] > 0) pq.add(new int[]{i, c[i]});
        StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder();
        int[] prev = null;
        while (!pq.isEmpty()) {
            int[] cur = pq.poll();
            sb.append((char) ('a' + cur[0]));
            if (prev != null && prev[1] > 0) pq.add(prev);
            cur[1]--;
            prev = cur;
        }
        return sb.length() == s.length() ? sb.toString() : "";
    }

    // Meeting Rooms II (LC 253): min-heap of end times
    static int minMeetingRooms(int[][] iv) {
        Arrays.sort(iv, (a, b) -> a[0] - b[0]);
        PriorityQueue<Integer> ends = new PriorityQueue<>();
        for (int[] i : iv) {
            if (!ends.isEmpty() && ends.peek() <= i[0]) ends.poll();
            ends.add(i[1]);
        }
        return ends.size();
    }

    // IPO (LC 502): sort by capital, max-heap of affordable profits
    static int findMaximizedCapital(int k, int w, int[] profits, int[] capital) {
        int n = profits.length;
        Integer[] idx = new Integer[n];
        for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) idx[i] = i;
        Arrays.sort(idx, Comparator.comparingInt(i -> capital[i]));
        PriorityQueue<Integer> pq = new PriorityQueue<>(Collections.reverseOrder());
        int p = 0;
        while (k-- > 0) {
            while (p < n && capital[idx[p]] <= w) pq.add(profits[idx[p++]]);
            if (pq.isEmpty()) break;
            w += pq.poll();
        }
        return w;
    }

    // Furthest Building You Can Reach (LC 1642): spend ladders on the biggest gaps (min-heap of ladder gaps)
    static int furthestBuilding(int[] h, int bricks, int ladders) {
        PriorityQueue<Integer> used = new PriorityQueue<>();
        for (int i = 0; i + 1 < h.length; i++) {
            int d = h[i + 1] - h[i];
            if (d <= 0) continue;
            used.add(d);
            if (used.size() > ladders) bricks -= used.poll();
            if (bricks < 0) return i;
        }
        return h.length - 1;
    }

    // Ugly Number II (LC 264): three pointers (heap-free)
    static int nthUglyNumber(int n) {
        int[] u = new int[n];
        u[0] = 1;
        int i2 = 0, i3 = 0, i5 = 0;
        for (int i = 1; i < n; i++) {
            int next = Math.min(u[i2] * 2, Math.min(u[i3] * 3, u[i5] * 5));
            u[i] = next;
            if (next == u[i2] * 2) i2++;
            if (next == u[i3] * 3) i3++;
            if (next == u[i5] * 5) i5++;
        }
        return u[n - 1];
    }

    // Lazy-deletion heap pattern: remember what is deleted in a map, discard stale tops when peeking.
    // (see Dijkstra "if (d > dist[u]) continue" in the graphs topic -- same idea)
}

Pitfalls

  1. Heap of size K for K largest is a MIN-heap; people reach for a max-heap by reflex.
  2. PriorityQueue has no decrease-key: push duplicates and skip stale entries on pop.
  3. Comparator subtraction can overflow; use Integer.compare for large values.
35 — HEAPSVARIANTS.JAVA

Heaps: Hard Variants

The senior-level heap problems add one twist to the basic Top-K: a ratio sort first, removal from the middle, a decrease-key, or a boundary that expands from its lowest point. Learn to spot which twist it is.

PatternUse caseComplexity
Sort + heapPick k items minimizing a ratio-weighted costO(n log n)
Two ordered setsMedian or order statistic of a sliding window (needs removal)O(n log k)
Indexed PQDecrease-key for Dijkstra / PrimO(log n) per update
Boundary heap3D flooding: always expand from the lowest wallO(mn log mn)
Deadline + max-heapSchedule maximum tasks, evict the longestO(n log n)
HeapsVariants.java
Sliding window median (two TreeSets), min cost to hire workers, max performance, k smallest pairs, kth smallest prime fraction, course schedule III, connect sticks, trapping rain water II, single-threaded CPU, minimum deviation, KthLargest stream, indexed min-PQ with decrease-key
Hard variants 
import java.util.*;

public class HeapsVariants {

    // ---------- Sliding Window Median, O(n log k): two TreeSets of INDICES ordered by (value, index) (LC 480) ----------
    // RECOGNIZE: need median / order statistic of a moving window with deletions. Heaps cannot delete arbitrary items; ordered sets can.
    static double[] medianSlidingWindowTwoSets(int[] a, int k) {
        Comparator<Integer> cmp = (i, j) -> a[i] != a[j] ? Integer.compare(a[i], a[j]) : Integer.compare(i, j);
        TreeSet<Integer> lo = new TreeSet<>(cmp), hi = new TreeSet<>(cmp); // lo holds the lower half (size = ceil(k/2))
        double[] res = new double[a.length - k + 1];
        for (int i = 0; i < a.length; i++) {
            if (lo.isEmpty() || cmp.compare(i, lo.last()) <= 0) lo.add(i); else hi.add(i);
            if (i >= k) { int out = i - k; if (!lo.remove(out)) hi.remove(out); }
            while (lo.size() > hi.size() + 1) hi.add(lo.pollLast());
            while (lo.size() < hi.size()) lo.add(hi.pollFirst());
            if (i >= k - 1) res[i - k + 1] = k % 2 == 1 ? a[lo.last()] : ((double) a[lo.last()] + a[hi.first()]) / 2;
        }
        return res;
    }

    // ---------- Minimum Cost to Hire K Workers (LC 857): sort by wage/quality; keep the k smallest qualities ----------
    // Paying everyone at the group's max ratio makes cost = ratio * sumQuality; minimize both with a max-heap of quality.
    static double mincostToHireWorkers(int[] quality, int[] wage, int k) {
        int n = quality.length;
        Integer[] idx = new Integer[n];
        for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) idx[i] = i;
        Arrays.sort(idx, (x, y) -> Double.compare((double) wage[x] / quality[x], (double) wage[y] / quality[y]));
        PriorityQueue<Integer> pq = new PriorityQueue<>(Collections.reverseOrder());
        long sum = 0;
        double best = Double.MAX_VALUE;
        for (int i : idx) {
            pq.add(quality[i]);
            sum += quality[i];
            if (pq.size() > k) sum -= pq.poll();
            if (pq.size() == k) best = Math.min(best, sum * ((double) wage[i] / quality[i]));
        }
        return best;
    }

    // ---------- Maximum Performance of a Team (LC 1383): sort by efficiency desc, min-heap of speeds of size k ----------
    static int maxPerformance(int n, int[] speed, int[] eff, int k) {
        Integer[] idx = new Integer[n];
        for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) idx[i] = i;
        Arrays.sort(idx, (a, b) -> eff[b] - eff[a]);
        PriorityQueue<Integer> pq = new PriorityQueue<>();
        long sum = 0, best = 0;
        for (int i : idx) {
            pq.add(speed[i]);
            sum += speed[i];
            if (pq.size() > k) sum -= pq.poll();
            best = Math.max(best, sum * eff[i]);
        }
        return (int) (best % 1_000_000_007L);
    }

    // ---------- Find K Pairs with Smallest Sums (LC 373): frontier heap over (i, j) ----------
    static List<List<Integer>> kSmallestPairs(int[] a, int[] b, int k) {
        List<List<Integer>> res = new ArrayList<>();
        if (a.length == 0 || b.length == 0) return res;
        PriorityQueue<int[]> pq = new PriorityQueue<>((x, y) -> Integer.compare(a[x[0]] + b[x[1]], a[y[0]] + b[y[1]]));
        for (int i = 0; i < Math.min(a.length, k); i++) pq.add(new int[]{i, 0});
        while (k-- > 0 && !pq.isEmpty()) {
            int[] t = pq.poll();
            res.add(List.of(a[t[0]], b[t[1]]));
            if (t[1] + 1 < b.length) pq.add(new int[]{t[0], t[1] + 1});
        }
        return res;
    }

    // ---------- K-th Smallest Prime Fraction (LC 786): frontier heap, compare fractions by cross-multiplication ----------
    static int[] kthSmallestPrimeFraction(int[] arr, int k) {
        int n = arr.length;
        PriorityQueue<int[]> pq = new PriorityQueue<>((x, y) -> Long.compare((long) arr[x[0]] * arr[y[1]], (long) arr[y[0]] * arr[x[1]]));
        for (int j = 1; j < n; j++) pq.add(new int[]{0, j}); // numerator index i, denominator index j
        while (--k > 0) {
            int[] t = pq.poll();
            if (t[0] + 1 < t[1]) pq.add(new int[]{t[0] + 1, t[1]});
        }
        int[] t = pq.peek();
        return new int[]{arr[t[0]], arr[t[1]]};
    }

    // ---------- Course Schedule III (LC 630): sort by deadline; if over time, drop the LONGEST course taken ----------
    // Exchange argument: swapping the longest taken course for a shorter new one never hurts.
    static int scheduleCourse(int[][] courses) {
        Arrays.sort(courses, (a, b) -> a[1] - b[1]);
        PriorityQueue<Integer> pq = new PriorityQueue<>(Collections.reverseOrder());
        int time = 0;
        for (int[] c : courses) {
            pq.add(c[0]);
            time += c[0];
            if (time > c[1]) time -= pq.poll();
        }
        return pq.size();
    }

    // ---------- Minimum Cost to Connect Sticks (LC 1167) / Huffman: always merge the two smallest ----------
    static int connectSticks(int[] sticks) {
        PriorityQueue<Integer> pq = new PriorityQueue<>();
        for (int s : sticks) pq.add(s);
        int cost = 0;
        while (pq.size() > 1) {
            int m = pq.poll() + pq.poll();
            cost += m;
            pq.add(m);
        }
        return cost;
    }

    // ---------- Trapping Rain Water II (LC 407): flood from the lowest boundary cell inward ----------
    static int trapRainWater(int[][] h) {
        int m = h.length, n = h[0].length;
        if (m < 3 || n < 3) return 0;
        boolean[][] seen = new boolean[m][n];
        PriorityQueue<int[]> pq = new PriorityQueue<>((a, b) -> a[0] - b[0]); // {height, r, c}
        for (int i = 0; i < m; i++)
            for (int j = 0; j < n; j++)
                if (i == 0 || j == 0 || i == m - 1 || j == n - 1) { pq.add(new int[]{h[i][j], i, j}); seen[i][j] = true; }
        int water = 0;
        int[] d = {0, 1, 0, -1, 0};
        while (!pq.isEmpty()) {
            int[] t = pq.poll();
            for (int k = 0; k < 4; k++) {
                int r = t[1] + d[k], c = t[2] + d[k + 1];
                if (r < 0 || c < 0 || r >= m || c >= n || seen[r][c]) continue;
                seen[r][c] = true;
                water += Math.max(0, t[0] - h[r][c]);
                pq.add(new int[]{Math.max(t[0], h[r][c]), r, c}); // level rises to the wall
            }
        }
        return water;
    }

    // ---------- Single-Threaded CPU (LC 1834): sort by enqueue time, heap of available by (processing time, index) ----------
    static int[] getOrder(int[][] tasks) {
        int n = tasks.length;
        Integer[] byStart = new Integer[n];
        for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) byStart[i] = i;
        Arrays.sort(byStart, (a, b) -> tasks[a][0] - tasks[b][0]);
        PriorityQueue<Integer> ready = new PriorityQueue<>((a, b) -> tasks[a][1] != tasks[b][1] ? tasks[a][1] - tasks[b][1] : a - b);
        int[] order = new int[n];
        long time = 0;
        int p = 0, o = 0;
        while (o < n) {
            if (ready.isEmpty() && time < tasks[byStart[p]][0]) time = tasks[byStart[p]][0]; // CPU idle: jump ahead
            while (p < n && tasks[byStart[p]][0] <= time) ready.add(byStart[p++]);
            int t = ready.poll();
            order[o++] = t;
            time += tasks[t][1];
        }
        return order;
    }

    // ---------- Minimize Deviation in Array (LC 1675): odds can only double, evens can only halve ----------
    // Double every odd once (now only halving remains), then repeatedly halve the max while it is even.
    static int minimumDeviation(int[] nums) {
        PriorityQueue<Integer> pq = new PriorityQueue<>(Collections.reverseOrder());
        int min = Integer.MAX_VALUE;
        for (int x : nums) {
            if (x % 2 == 1) x *= 2;
            pq.add(x);
            min = Math.min(min, x);
        }
        int best = pq.peek() - min;
        while (pq.peek() % 2 == 0) {
            int mx = pq.poll() / 2;
            pq.add(mx);
            min = Math.min(min, mx);
            best = Math.min(best, pq.peek() - min);
        }
        return best;
    }

    // ---------- Kth Largest Element in a Stream (LC 703) ----------
    static class KthLargest {
        private final PriorityQueue<Integer> pq = new PriorityQueue<>();
        private final int k;
        KthLargest(int k, int[] nums) { this.k = k; for (int x : nums) add(x); }
        int add(int v) { pq.add(v); if (pq.size() > k) pq.poll(); return pq.peek(); }
    }

    // ---------- Indexed min-priority-queue with decrease-key ----------
    // RECOGNIZE: Dijkstra / Prim written with a true decrease-key instead of "push duplicates and skip stale".
    static class IndexedMinPQ {
        private final int[] heap, pos; // heap[i] = item id; pos[id] = index in heap or -1
        private final long[] key;
        private int size;
        IndexedMinPQ(int capacity) {
            heap = new int[capacity];
            pos = new int[capacity];
            key = new long[capacity];
            Arrays.fill(pos, -1);
        }
        boolean contains(int id) { return pos[id] != -1; }
        boolean isEmpty() { return size == 0; }
        void insert(int id, long k) { key[id] = k; heap[size] = id; pos[id] = size; up(size++); }
        void decreaseKey(int id, long k) { if (k < key[id]) { key[id] = k; up(pos[id]); } }
        int extractMin() {
            int top = heap[0];
            swap(0, --size);
            pos[top] = -1;
            if (size > 0) down(0);
            return top;
        }
        long keyOf(int id) { return key[id]; }
        private void up(int i) { while (i > 0 && key[heap[i]] < key[heap[(i - 1) / 2]]) { swap(i, (i - 1) / 2); i = (i - 1) / 2; } }
        private void down(int i) {
            while (true) {
                int l = 2 * i + 1, r = l + 1, s = i;
                if (l < size && key[heap[l]] < key[heap[s]]) s = l;
                if (r < size && key[heap[r]] < key[heap[s]]) s = r;
                if (s == i) return;
                swap(i, s);
                i = s;
            }
        }
        private void swap(int i, int j) {
            int t = heap[i]; heap[i] = heap[j]; heap[j] = t;
            pos[heap[i]] = i;
            pos[heap[j]] = j;
        }
    }
}

Pitfalls

  1. A PriorityQueue cannot remove from the middle in O(log n); use TreeSet of (value, index) pairs when a window slides.
  2. Ratio problems: sort by the ratio first, then the heap holds the quantity you want to drop.
  3. Duplicate values in a TreeSet collapse; key by index, or by (value, index).
36 — INTERVALS.JAVA

Intervals & Sweep Line

First decide the sort key: by START for merging, inserting and overlap counting; by END for "keep the most / fewest arrows" greedy. Sweep line turns intervals into +1/-1 events; TreeMap handles online booking.

PatternUse caseComplexity
Merge / insertSort by start, extend the last output intervalO(n log n)
Max non-overlappingSort by END, keep the earliest finisherO(n log n)
Sweep line+1 at start, -1 at end, track the running maxO(n log n)
Online bookingTreeMap floor / ceiling checksO(log n)
Intervals.java
Merge, insert, non-overlapping, arrows, intersections, meeting rooms, sweep, car pooling, calendar I/III, employee free time, covered intervals, summary ranges
O(n log n) 
import java.util.*;

public class Intervals {

    // ALWAYS first decide: sort by START (merge, insert, overlaps) or by END (max non-overlapping, min arrows).

    // Merge Intervals (LC 56)
    static int[][] merge(int[][] iv) {
        Arrays.sort(iv, (a, b) -> Integer.compare(a[0], b[0]));
        List<int[]> out = new ArrayList<>();
        for (int[] cur : iv) {
            if (out.isEmpty() || out.get(out.size() - 1)[1] < cur[0]) out.add(cur.clone());
            else out.get(out.size() - 1)[1] = Math.max(out.get(out.size() - 1)[1], cur[1]);
        }
        return out.toArray(new int[0][]);
    }

    // Insert Interval (LC 57): before / overlapping / after, one pass
    static int[][] insert(int[][] iv, int[] add) {
        List<int[]> out = new ArrayList<>();
        int i = 0, n = iv.length;
        while (i < n && iv[i][1] < add[0]) out.add(iv[i++]);
        int[] cur = add.clone();
        while (i < n && iv[i][0] <= cur[1]) { cur[0] = Math.min(cur[0], iv[i][0]); cur[1] = Math.max(cur[1], iv[i][1]); i++; }
        out.add(cur);
        while (i < n) out.add(iv[i++]);
        return out.toArray(new int[0][]);
    }

    // Non-overlapping Intervals (LC 435): keep the interval with the EARLIEST END; count removals
    static int eraseOverlapIntervals(int[][] iv) {
        Arrays.sort(iv, (a, b) -> Integer.compare(a[1], b[1]));
        int removed = 0, end = Integer.MIN_VALUE;
        for (int[] x : iv) {
            if (x[0] >= end) end = x[1]; else removed++;
        }
        return removed;
    }

    // Minimum Arrows to Burst Balloons (LC 452): sort by end, one arrow per cluster
    static int findMinArrowShots(int[][] pts) {
        Arrays.sort(pts, (a, b) -> Integer.compare(a[1], b[1]));
        int arrows = 0;
        long end = Long.MIN_VALUE;
        for (int[] p : pts) if (p[0] > end) { arrows++; end = p[1]; }
        return arrows;
    }

    // Interval List Intersections (LC 986): two pointers, advance the one that ends first
    static int[][] intervalIntersection(int[][] a, int[][] b) {
        List<int[]> out = new ArrayList<>();
        int i = 0, j = 0;
        while (i < a.length && j < b.length) {
            int lo = Math.max(a[i][0], b[j][0]), hi = Math.min(a[i][1], b[j][1]);
            if (lo <= hi) out.add(new int[]{lo, hi});
            if (a[i][1] < b[j][1]) i++; else j++;
        }
        return out.toArray(new int[0][]);
    }

    // Meeting Rooms (LC 252): any overlap?
    static boolean canAttendMeetings(int[][] iv) {
        Arrays.sort(iv, (a, b) -> a[0] - b[0]);
        for (int i = 1; i < iv.length; i++) if (iv[i][0] < iv[i - 1][1]) return false;
        return true;
    }

    // ---------- Sweep line with events: max concurrent overlap (rooms) ----------
    // Ends sort BEFORE starts at the same time when [s, e) is half-open.
    static int maxOverlap(int[][] iv) {
        int[] starts = new int[iv.length], ends = new int[iv.length];
        for (int i = 0; i < iv.length; i++) { starts[i] = iv[i][0]; ends[i] = iv[i][1]; }
        Arrays.sort(starts);
        Arrays.sort(ends);
        int e = 0, cur = 0, best = 0;
        for (int s : starts) {
            while (ends[e] <= s) { e++; cur--; }
            cur++;
            best = Math.max(best, cur);
        }
        return best;
    }

    // Car Pooling (LC 1094): difference array over positions
    static boolean carPooling(int[][] trips, int capacity) {
        int[] diff = new int[1002];
        for (int[] t : trips) { diff[t[1]] += t[0]; diff[t[2]] -= t[0]; }
        int cur = 0;
        for (int d : diff) { cur += d; if (cur > capacity) return false; }
        return true;
    }

    // My Calendar I (LC 729): TreeMap floor / ceiling check
    static class MyCalendar {
        private final TreeMap<Integer, Integer> m = new TreeMap<>(); // start -> end
        boolean book(int s, int e) {
            Integer prev = m.floorKey(s), next = m.ceilingKey(s);
            if ((prev != null && m.get(prev) > s) || (next != null && next < e)) return false;
            m.put(s, e);
            return true;
        }
    }

    // My Calendar III (LC 732): max k-booking via TreeMap of +1 / -1 deltas
    static class MyCalendarThree {
        private final TreeMap<Integer, Integer> delta = new TreeMap<>();
        int book(int s, int e) {
            delta.merge(s, 1, Integer::sum);
            delta.merge(e, -1, Integer::sum);
            int cur = 0, best = 0;
            for (int d : delta.values()) { cur += d; best = Math.max(best, cur); }
            return best;
        }
    }

    // Employee Free Time (LC 759): merge all busy intervals, gaps are free
    static List<int[]> employeeFreeTime(List<List<int[]>> schedule) {
        List<int[]> all = new ArrayList<>();
        for (List<int[]> s : schedule) all.addAll(s);
        all.sort((a, b) -> a[0] - b[0]);
        List<int[]> free = new ArrayList<>();
        int end = all.get(0)[1];
        for (int[] x : all) {
            if (x[0] > end) free.add(new int[]{end, x[0]});
            end = Math.max(end, x[1]);
        }
        return free;
    }

    // Remove Covered Intervals (LC 1288)
    static int removeCoveredIntervals(int[][] iv) {
        Arrays.sort(iv, (a, b) -> a[0] != b[0] ? a[0] - b[0] : b[1] - a[1]);
        int count = 0, maxEnd = 0;
        for (int[] x : iv) if (x[1] > maxEnd) { count++; maxEnd = x[1]; }
        return count;
    }

    // Data Stream as Disjoint Intervals (LC 352)
    static class SummaryRanges {
        private final TreeMap<Integer, Integer> m = new TreeMap<>(); // start -> end
        void addNum(int v) {
            Integer lo = m.floorKey(v);
            if (lo != null && m.get(lo) >= v) return;
            boolean joinLeft = lo != null && m.get(lo) == v - 1, joinRight = m.containsKey(v + 1);
            if (joinLeft && joinRight) { m.put(lo, m.remove(v + 1)); }
            else if (joinLeft) m.put(lo, v);
            else if (joinRight) { m.put(v, m.remove(v + 1)); }
            else m.put(v, v);
        }
        int[][] getIntervals() {
            int[][] r = new int[m.size()][];
            int i = 0;
            for (Map.Entry<Integer, Integer> e : m.entrySet()) r[i++] = new int[]{e.getKey(), e.getValue()};
            return r;
        }
    }
}

Pitfalls

  1. Half-open [s, e): process ends before starts at the same timestamp.
  2. Touching intervals: decide up front whether [1,2] and [2,3] overlap.
  3. Insert interval needs no sort when the input is already sorted: three phases in one pass.

Intervals: Sweeps & Cover

Harder interval problems combine a sort with a heap or a TreeMap, or ask for a minimum cover. Decide whether you sweep by start, by end, or by day.

PatternUse caseComplexity
Offline queriesSmallest interval containing each queryO((n + q) log n)
Day sweep + heapAttend the most events, one per dayO(n log n)
Greedy coverFewest clips / taps to cover a rangeO(n)
TreeMap of rangesAdd / remove / query covered ranges dynamicallyO(log n) amortized
Sweep lineUnion area of rectanglesO(n² ) or O(n log n)

Hard variants 
import java.util.*;

public class IntervalsVariants {

    // ---------- Minimum Interval to Include Each Query (LC 1851): offline, sort queries, heap by (size, end) ----------
    // RECOGNIZE: many point queries against many intervals, answers need not be online -> sort both and sweep.
    static int[] minInterval(int[][] intervals, int[] queries) {
        Arrays.sort(intervals, (a, b) -> a[0] - b[0]);
        int q = queries.length;
        Integer[] order = new Integer[q];
        for (int i = 0; i < q; i++) order[i] = i;
        Arrays.sort(order, (a, b) -> queries[a] - queries[b]);
        PriorityQueue<int[]> pq = new PriorityQueue<>((a, b) -> a[0] != b[0] ? a[0] - b[0] : a[1] - b[1]); // {size, end}
        int[] ans = new int[q];
        int p = 0;
        for (int qi : order) {
            int x = queries[qi];
            while (p < intervals.length && intervals[p][0] <= x) { pq.add(new int[]{intervals[p][1] - intervals[p][0] + 1, intervals[p][1]}); p++; }
            while (!pq.isEmpty() && pq.peek()[1] < x) pq.poll(); // lazily drop intervals that already ended
            ans[qi] = pq.isEmpty() ? -1 : pq.peek()[0];
        }
        return ans;
    }

    // ---------- Maximum Number of Events You Can Attend (LC 1353): each day attend the event that ends soonest ----------
    static int maxEvents(int[][] events) {
        Arrays.sort(events, (a, b) -> a[0] - b[0]);
        PriorityQueue<Integer> ends = new PriorityQueue<>();
        int i = 0, day = 0, count = 0, n = events.length;
        while (i < n || !ends.isEmpty()) {
            if (ends.isEmpty()) day = events[i][0];
            while (i < n && events[i][0] <= day) ends.add(events[i++][1]);
            while (!ends.isEmpty() && ends.peek() < day) ends.poll();
            if (!ends.isEmpty()) { ends.poll(); count++; }
            day++;
        }
        return count;
    }

    // ---------- Meeting Rooms III (LC 2402): free-room heap + busy heap (end, room) ----------
    static int mostBooked(int n, int[][] meetings) {
        Arrays.sort(meetings, (a, b) -> a[0] - b[0]);
        PriorityQueue<Integer> free = new PriorityQueue<>();
        for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) free.add(i);
        PriorityQueue<long[]> busy = new PriorityQueue<>((a, b) -> a[0] != b[0] ? Long.compare(a[0], b[0]) : Long.compare(a[1], b[1]));
        int[] used = new int[n];
        for (int[] m : meetings) {
            while (!busy.isEmpty() && busy.peek()[0] <= m[0]) free.add((int) busy.poll()[1]);
            if (!free.isEmpty()) {
                int r = free.poll();
                used[r]++;
                busy.add(new long[]{m[1], r});
            } else {
                long[] t = busy.poll(); // wait for the earliest room, meeting keeps its duration
                used[(int) t[1]]++;
                busy.add(new long[]{t[0] + (m[1] - m[0]), t[1]});
            }
        }
        int best = 0;
        for (int i = 1; i < n; i++) if (used[i] > used[best]) best = i;
        return best;
    }

    // ---------- Divide Intervals Into Minimum Number of Groups (LC 2406) ----------
    static int minGroups(int[][] intervals) {
        Arrays.sort(intervals, (a, b) -> a[0] - b[0]);
        PriorityQueue<Integer> ends = new PriorityQueue<>();
        for (int[] iv : intervals) {
            if (!ends.isEmpty() && ends.peek() < iv[0]) ends.poll(); // closed intervals: touching at a point conflicts
            ends.add(iv[1]);
        }
        return ends.size();
    }

    // ---------- Video Stitching (LC 1024) / Minimum Taps (LC 1326): jump-game on intervals ----------
    // Normalize to "furthest right end reachable from each left start", then run Jump Game II.
    static int videoStitching(int[][] clips, int time) {
        int[] far = new int[time + 1];
        for (int[] c : clips) if (c[0] <= time) far[c[0]] = Math.max(far[c[0]], Math.min(c[1], time));
        int count = 0, curEnd = 0, reach = 0;
        for (int i = 0; i < time; i++) {
            reach = Math.max(reach, far[i]);
            if (i == curEnd) {
                if (reach <= i) return -1;
                count++;
                curEnd = reach;
            }
        }
        return count;
    }

    static int minTaps(int n, int[] ranges) {
        int[] far = new int[n + 1];
        for (int i = 0; i <= n; i++) {
            int l = Math.max(0, i - ranges[i]), r = Math.min(n, i + ranges[i]);
            far[l] = Math.max(far[l], r);
        }
        int taps = 0, curEnd = 0, reach = 0;
        for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
            reach = Math.max(reach, far[i]);
            if (i == curEnd) {
                if (reach <= i) return -1;
                taps++;
                curEnd = reach;
            }
        }
        return taps;
    }

    // ---------- Remove Interval (LC 1272): subtract [lo, hi) from a sorted disjoint list ----------
    static List<List<Integer>> removeInterval(int[][] iv, int[] rm) {
        List<List<Integer>> res = new ArrayList<>();
        for (int[] x : iv) {
            if (x[1] <= rm[0] || x[0] >= rm[1]) res.add(List.of(x[0], x[1]));
            else {
                if (x[0] < rm[0]) res.add(List.of(x[0], rm[0]));
                if (x[1] > rm[1]) res.add(List.of(rm[1], x[1]));
            }
        }
        return res;
    }

    // ---------- Range Module (LC 715): TreeMap of disjoint half-open ranges start -> end ----------
    static class RangeModule {
        private final TreeMap<Integer, Integer> m = new TreeMap<>();

        void addRange(int l, int r) {
            Map.Entry<Integer, Integer> e = m.floorEntry(l);
            if (e != null && e.getValue() >= l) { l = e.getKey(); r = Math.max(r, e.getValue()); } // touching ranges merge
            while (true) {
                Map.Entry<Integer, Integer> n = m.ceilingEntry(l);
                if (n == null || n.getKey() > r) break;
                r = Math.max(r, n.getValue());
                m.remove(n.getKey());
            }
            m.put(l, r);
        }

        boolean queryRange(int l, int r) {
            Map.Entry<Integer, Integer> e = m.floorEntry(l);
            return e != null && e.getValue() >= r;
        }

        void removeRange(int l, int r) {
            Map.Entry<Integer, Integer> e = m.lowerEntry(l);
            if (e != null && e.getValue() > l) { // left piece survives
                int end = e.getValue();
                m.put(e.getKey(), l);
                if (end > r) m.put(r, end);
            }
            while (true) {
                Map.Entry<Integer, Integer> n = m.ceilingEntry(l);
                if (n == null || n.getKey() >= r) break;
                m.remove(n.getKey());
                if (n.getValue() > r) m.put(r, n.getValue());
            }
        }
    }

    // ---------- Rectangle Area II (LC 850): area of the union, sweep x with coordinate-compressed y coverage ----------
    static int rectangleArea(int[][] rects) {
        final long MOD = 1_000_000_007L;
        TreeSet<Integer> ys = new TreeSet<>();
        List<int[]> ev = new ArrayList<>(); // {x, +1/-1, y1, y2}
        for (int[] r : rects) {
            ys.add(r[1]); ys.add(r[3]);
            ev.add(new int[]{r[0], 1, r[1], r[3]});
            ev.add(new int[]{r[2], -1, r[1], r[3]});
        }
        ev.sort((a, b) -> a[0] - b[0]);
        Integer[] yv = ys.toArray(new Integer[0]);
        Map<Integer, Integer> id = new HashMap<>();
        for (int i = 0; i < yv.length; i++) id.put(yv[i], i);
        int[] cover = new int[yv.length];
        long area = 0;
        int prevX = ev.get(0)[0];
        for (int[] e : ev) {
            long covered = 0; // total covered y-length with the current multiset of active rectangles
            for (int i = 0; i + 1 < yv.length; i++) if (cover[i] > 0) covered += yv[i + 1] - yv[i];
            area = (area + covered % MOD * (e[0] - prevX)) % MOD;
            for (int i = id.get(e[2]); i < id.get(e[3]); i++) cover[i] += e[1];
            prevX = e[0];
        }
        return (int) area;
    }

    // ---------- Stabbing counts: how many intervals contain point p? Two sorted arrays, no tree needed ----------
    // count(start <= p) - count(end < p). Use for static data with many queries.
    static class StabbingCounter {
        private final int[] starts, ends;
        StabbingCounter(int[][] iv) {
            starts = new int[iv.length];
            ends = new int[iv.length];
            for (int i = 0; i < iv.length; i++) { starts[i] = iv[i][0]; ends[i] = iv[i][1]; }
            Arrays.sort(starts);
            Arrays.sort(ends);
        }
        int count(int p) { return upper(starts, p) - lower(ends, p); }
        private static int upper(int[] a, int x) { int lo = 0, hi = a.length; while (lo < hi) { int m = (lo + hi) >>> 1; if (a[m] > x) hi = m; else lo = m + 1; } return lo; }
        private static int lower(int[] a, int x) { int lo = 0, hi = a.length; while (lo < hi) { int m = (lo + hi) >>> 1; if (a[m] >= x) hi = m; else lo = m + 1; } return lo; }
    }
}

Pitfalls

  1. Sort queries and intervals together, offline; never answer queries in input order.
  2. Greedy cover: extend to the furthest reach among intervals starting at or before the current end.
  3. Half-open [l, r) intervals avoid off-by-one in touching ranges.
38 — BINARYSEARCH.JAVA

Binary Search

One template covers everything: find the FIRST index in [lo, hi] where a monotone predicate ok(i) becomes true, with `while (lo < hi)` and `hi = mid` on true. Searching on the answer is the same loop with ok(x) = "is x feasible?".

PatternUse caseComplexity
BoundslowerBound / upperBound, first and last positionO(log n)
Rotated arraysOne half is always sortedO(log n)
Search on answerMin speed / capacity / days such that feasibleO(n log range)
Partition searchMedian of two sorted arraysO(log min(m, n))
BinarySearch.java
Lower/upper bound, range, rotated search and min, peak, matrices, Koko, shipping, split array, bouquets, multiplication table, two-array median, sqrt, time map, K closest
O(log n) 
import java.util.*;

public class BinarySearch {

    // ===== THE ONE TEMPLATE: find the FIRST index in [lo, hi] where ok(i) is true (ok is monotone F..F T..T) =====
    //   lo = 0, hi = n (n means "none true"); while (lo < hi) { mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2; if (ok(mid)) hi = mid; else lo = mid + 1; }
    //   Every problem = choose the search space + write ok(). "Last true" = (first true of the negation) - 1.

    // lower bound: first index with a[i] >= x
    static int lowerBound(int[] a, int x) {
        int lo = 0, hi = a.length;
        while (lo < hi) {
            int mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2;
            if (a[mid] >= x) hi = mid; else lo = mid + 1;
        }
        return lo;
    }

    // upper bound: first index with a[i] > x
    static int upperBound(int[] a, int x) {
        int lo = 0, hi = a.length;
        while (lo < hi) {
            int mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2;
            if (a[mid] > x) hi = mid; else lo = mid + 1;
        }
        return lo;
    }

    // Find First and Last Position (LC 34)
    static int[] searchRange(int[] a, int target) {
        int l = lowerBound(a, target);
        if (l == a.length || a[l] != target) return new int[]{-1, -1};
        return new int[]{l, upperBound(a, target) - 1};
    }

    // Search Insert Position (LC 35)
    static int searchInsert(int[] a, int target) { return lowerBound(a, target); }

    // ---------- Rotated sorted array (LC 33, distinct): one half is always sorted ----------
    static int searchRotated(int[] a, int t) {
        int lo = 0, hi = a.length - 1;
        while (lo <= hi) {
            int mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2;
            if (a[mid] == t) return mid;
            if (a[lo] <= a[mid]) { // left half sorted
                if (a[lo] <= t && t < a[mid]) hi = mid - 1; else lo = mid + 1;
            } else {
                if (a[mid] < t && t <= a[hi]) lo = mid + 1; else hi = mid - 1;
            }
        }
        return -1;
    }

    // Find Minimum in Rotated Sorted Array (LC 153); duplicates (LC 154) shrink hi on ties
    static int findMin(int[] a) {
        int lo = 0, hi = a.length - 1;
        while (lo < hi) {
            int mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2;
            if (a[mid] > a[hi]) lo = mid + 1;
            else if (a[mid] < a[hi]) hi = mid;
            else hi--; // equal: cannot tell, shrink safely
        }
        return a[lo];
    }

    // Peak Element (LC 162): follow the uphill side
    static int findPeakElement(int[] a) {
        int lo = 0, hi = a.length - 1;
        while (lo < hi) {
            int mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2;
            if (a[mid] < a[mid + 1]) lo = mid + 1; else hi = mid;
        }
        return lo;
    }

    // Search a 2D Matrix (LC 74): treat as a flat sorted array
    static boolean searchMatrix(int[][] m, int t) {
        int R = m.length, C = m[0].length, lo = 0, hi = R * C - 1;
        while (lo <= hi) {
            int mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2, v = m[mid / C][mid % C];
            if (v == t) return true;
            if (v < t) lo = mid + 1; else hi = mid - 1;
        }
        return false;
    }

    // Search a 2D Matrix II (LC 240): staircase from the top-right, O(m + n)
    static boolean searchMatrixII(int[][] m, int t) {
        int r = 0, c = m[0].length - 1;
        while (r < m.length && c >= 0) {
            if (m[r][c] == t) return true;
            if (m[r][c] > t) c--; else r++;
        }
        return false;
    }

    // ===== BINARY SEARCH ON THE ANSWER: ok(x) = "is x enough / feasible?" =====
    // Koko Eating Bananas (LC 875): min speed finishing in h hours
    static int minEatingSpeed(int[] piles, int h) {
        int lo = 1, hi = Arrays.stream(piles).max().getAsInt();
        while (lo < hi) {
            int mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2;
            long hours = 0;
            for (int p : piles) hours += (p + mid - 1) / mid;
            if (hours <= h) hi = mid; else lo = mid + 1;
        }
        return lo;
    }

    // Capacity To Ship Packages Within D Days (LC 1011)
    static int shipWithinDays(int[] w, int days) {
        int lo = 0, hi = 0;
        for (int x : w) { lo = Math.max(lo, x); hi += x; }
        while (lo < hi) {
            int mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2, need = 1, cur = 0;
            for (int x : w) { if (cur + x > mid) { need++; cur = 0; } cur += x; }
            if (need <= days) hi = mid; else lo = mid + 1;
        }
        return lo;
    }

    // Split Array Largest Sum (LC 410): same shape as shipping
    static int splitArray(int[] a, int k) { return shipWithinDays(a, k); }

    // Minimum Days to Make m Bouquets (LC 1482)
    static int minDays(int[] bloom, int m, int k) {
        if ((long) m * k > bloom.length) return -1;
        int lo = 1, hi = Arrays.stream(bloom).max().getAsInt();
        while (lo < hi) {
            int mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2, bouquets = 0, run = 0;
            for (int b : bloom) {
                if (b <= mid) { if (++run == k) { bouquets++; run = 0; } } else run = 0;
            }
            if (bouquets >= m) hi = mid; else lo = mid + 1;
        }
        return lo;
    }

    // Kth Smallest in Multiplication Table (LC 668) / count-less-or-equal style
    static int findKthNumber(int m, int n, int k) {
        int lo = 1, hi = m * n;
        while (lo < hi) {
            int mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2, cnt = 0;
            for (int i = 1; i <= m; i++) cnt += Math.min(mid / i, n);
            if (cnt >= k) hi = mid; else lo = mid + 1;
        }
        return lo;
    }

    // Median of Two Sorted Arrays (LC 4): partition the smaller array, O(log min(m, n))
    static double findMedianSortedArrays(int[] a, int[] b) {
        if (a.length > b.length) return findMedianSortedArrays(b, a);
        int m = a.length, n = b.length, lo = 0, hi = m, half = (m + n + 1) / 2;
        while (lo <= hi) {
            int i = (lo + hi) / 2, j = half - i;
            int aL = i == 0 ? Integer.MIN_VALUE : a[i - 1], aR = i == m ? Integer.MAX_VALUE : a[i];
            int bL = j == 0 ? Integer.MIN_VALUE : b[j - 1], bR = j == n ? Integer.MAX_VALUE : b[j];
            if (aL <= bR && bL <= aR) {
                if ((m + n) % 2 == 1) return Math.max(aL, bL);
                return (Math.max(aL, bL) + (double) Math.min(aR, bR)) / 2;
            }
            if (aL > bR) hi = i - 1; else lo = i + 1;
        }
        throw new IllegalArgumentException();
    }

    // Real-valued search: sqrt with fixed iterations (avoids epsilon traps)
    static double sqrt(double x) {
        double lo = 0, hi = Math.max(1, x);
        for (int it = 0; it < 100; it++) {
            double mid = (lo + hi) / 2;
            if (mid * mid >= x) hi = mid; else lo = mid;
        }
        return hi;
    }

    // Integer sqrt (LC 69): last x with x*x <= n
    static int mySqrt(int n) {
        int lo = 0, hi = 46341; // 46341^2 overflows int, so it is the first "too big"
        while (lo < hi) {
            int mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2;
            if ((long) mid * mid > n) hi = mid; else lo = mid + 1;
        }
        return lo - 1;
    }

    // Time Based Key-Value Store (LC 981): binary search the latest timestamp <= t
    static class TimeMap {
        private final Map<String, List<int[]>> ts = new HashMap<>(); // {timestamp, valueIndex}
        private final List<String> vals = new ArrayList<>();
        void set(String k, String v, int t) {
            vals.add(v);
            ts.computeIfAbsent(k, x -> new ArrayList<>()).add(new int[]{t, vals.size() - 1});
        }
        String get(String k, int t) {
            List<int[]> l = ts.get(k);
            if (l == null) return "";
            int lo = 0, hi = l.size();
            while (lo < hi) {
                int mid = (lo + hi) >>> 1;
                if (l.get(mid)[0] > t) hi = mid; else lo = mid + 1;
            }
            return lo == 0 ? "" : vals.get(l.get(lo - 1)[1]);
        }
    }

    // Find K Closest Elements (LC 658): binary search the left edge of the window
    static List<Integer> findClosestElements(int[] a, int k, int x) {
        int lo = 0, hi = a.length - k;
        while (lo < hi) {
            int mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2;
            if (x - a[mid] > a[mid + k] - x) lo = mid + 1; else hi = mid;
        }
        List<Integer> res = new ArrayList<>();
        for (int i = lo; i < lo + k; i++) res.add(a[i]);
        return res;
    }
}

Pitfalls

  1. Compute mid as lo + (hi - lo) / 2 to avoid overflow.
  2. Search-on-answer needs a monotone predicate: if feasible(x) does not imply feasible(x + 1) you cannot binary search.
  3. With duplicates in a rotated array, equal ends force a linear shrink (worst case O(n)).
