import java.util.*;

public class BinarySearchVariants {

    // All of these are the same loop: pick the search space, write ok(x), find the first x where ok is true.

    // ---------- Find K-th Smallest Pair Distance (LC 719): count pairs with distance <= d using two pointers ----------
    static int smallestDistancePair(int[] a, int k) {
        Arrays.sort(a);
        int lo = 0, hi = a[a.length - 1] - a[0];
        while (lo < hi) {
            int mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2, count = 0, l = 0;
            for (int r = 0; r < a.length; r++) {
                while (a[r] - a[l] > mid) l++;
                count += r - l;
            }
            if (count >= k) hi = mid; else lo = mid + 1;
        }
        return lo;
    }

    // ---------- Smallest Divisor Given a Threshold (LC 1283) ----------
    static int smallestDivisor(int[] a, int threshold) {
        int lo = 1, hi = Arrays.stream(a).max().getAsInt();
        while (lo < hi) {
            int mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2;
            long sum = 0;
            for (int x : a) sum += (x + mid - 1) / mid;
            if (sum <= threshold) hi = mid; else lo = mid + 1;
        }
        return lo;
    }

    // ---------- Magnetic Force Between Two Balls / Aggressive Cows (LC 1552): maximize the minimum gap ----------
    // "Maximize the minimum": ok(d) = can we place m items at least d apart? ok is true then false, so search the LAST true.
    static int maxDistance(int[] position, int m) {
        Arrays.sort(position);
        int lo = 1, hi = position[position.length - 1] - position[0];
        while (lo < hi) {
            int mid = lo + (hi - lo + 1) / 2; // round up so the loop always shrinks
            int placed = 1, last = position[0];
            for (int p : position) if (p - last >= mid) { placed++; last = p; }
            if (placed >= m) lo = mid; else hi = mid - 1;
        }
        return lo;
    }

    // ---------- Minimize Max Distance to Gas Station (LC 774): real-valued search with a fixed iteration count ----------
    static double minmaxGasDist(int[] stations, int k) {
        double lo = 0, hi = stations[stations.length - 1] - stations[0];
        for (int it = 0; it < 100; it++) {
            double mid = (lo + hi) / 2;
            long need = 0;
            for (int i = 1; i < stations.length; i++) need += (long) Math.ceil((stations[i] - stations[i - 1]) / mid) - 1;
            if (need <= k) hi = mid; else lo = mid;
        }
        return hi;
    }

    // ---------- Kth Missing Positive Number (LC 1539): missing count before index i is a[i] - (i + 1), monotone ----------
    static int findKthPositive(int[] a, int k) {
        int lo = 0, hi = a.length;
        while (lo < hi) {
            int mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2;
            if (a[mid] - (mid + 1) >= k) hi = mid; else lo = mid + 1;
        }
        return lo + k;
    }

    // ---------- Single Element in a Sorted Array (LC 540): pairs start at even indices until the single element ----------
    static int singleNonDuplicate(int[] a) {
        int lo = 0, hi = a.length - 1;
        while (lo < hi) {
            int mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2;
            if (mid % 2 == 1) mid--; // align to an even index
            if (a[mid] == a[mid + 1]) lo = mid + 2; else hi = mid;
        }
        return a[lo];
    }

    // ---------- Maximum Value at a Given Index in a Bounded Array (LC 1802): sum of a triangle shape is monotone in the peak ----------
    static int maxValue(int n, int index, int maxSum) {
        int lo = 1, hi = maxSum;
        while (lo < hi) {
            int mid = lo + (hi - lo + 1) / 2;
            if (minSum(mid, index, n) <= maxSum) lo = mid; else hi = mid - 1;
        }
        return lo;
    }

    private static long minSum(long peak, int index, int n) {
        return side(peak, index + 1) + side(peak, n - index) - peak; // peak counted twice
    }

    private static long side(long peak, int len) { // peak, peak-1, ... down to 1 then ones
        if (peak >= len) return (peak + peak - len + 1) * len / 2;
        return peak * (peak + 1) / 2 + (len - peak);
    }

    // ---------- Minimum Time to Complete Trips (LC 2187) ----------
    static long minimumTime(int[] time, int totalTrips) {
        long lo = 1, hi = (long) Arrays.stream(time).min().getAsInt() * totalTrips;
        while (lo < hi) {
            long mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2, trips = 0;
            for (int t : time) trips += mid / t;
            if (trips >= totalTrips) hi = mid; else lo = mid + 1;
        }
        return lo;
    }

    // ---------- Minimize the Maximum Difference of Pairs (LC 2616): greedy pairing check inside the binary search ----------
    static int minimizeMax(int[] a, int p) {
        Arrays.sort(a);
        int lo = 0, hi = a[a.length - 1] - a[0];
        while (lo < hi) {
            int mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2, pairs = 0;
            for (int i = 1; i < a.length; i++) if (a[i] - a[i - 1] <= mid) { pairs++; i++; } // pair adjacent values greedily
            if (pairs >= p) hi = mid; else lo = mid + 1;
        }
        return lo;
    }

    // ---------- H-Index II (LC 275): citations sorted ascending ----------
    static int hIndex(int[] c) {
        int n = c.length, lo = 0, hi = n;
        while (lo < hi) {
            int mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2;
            if (c[mid] >= n - mid) hi = mid; else lo = mid + 1;
        }
        return n - lo;
    }

    // ---------- Find Right Interval (LC 436): sort starts, lower-bound each end ----------
    static int[] findRightInterval(int[][] iv) {
        int n = iv.length;
        Integer[] byStart = new Integer[n];
        for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) byStart[i] = i;
        Arrays.sort(byStart, (a, b) -> iv[a][0] - iv[b][0]);
        int[] res = new int[n];
        for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
            int lo = 0, hi = n;
            while (lo < hi) {
                int mid = (lo + hi) >>> 1;
                if (iv[byStart[mid]][0] >= iv[i][1]) hi = mid; else lo = mid + 1;
            }
            res[i] = lo == n ? -1 : byStart[lo];
        }
        return res;
    }

    // ---------- Max Sum of Rectangle No Larger Than K (LC 363): fix column pair, compress to 1D, prefix sums + TreeSet.ceiling ----------
    static int maxSumSubmatrix(int[][] m, int k) {
        int R = m.length, C = m[0].length, best = Integer.MIN_VALUE;
        for (int c1 = 0; c1 < C; c1++) {
            int[] rowSum = new int[R];
            for (int c2 = c1; c2 < C; c2++) {
                for (int r = 0; r < R; r++) rowSum[r] += m[r][c2];
                TreeSet<Integer> prefixes = new TreeSet<>();
                prefixes.add(0);
                int pre = 0;
                for (int r = 0; r < R; r++) {
                    pre += rowSum[r];
                    Integer need = prefixes.ceiling(pre - k); // smallest earlier prefix with pre - prefix <= k
                    if (need != null) best = Math.max(best, pre - need);
                    prefixes.add(pre);
                }
            }
        }
        return best;
    }

    // ---------- Search in a Bitonic / Mountain array: find the peak, then search each side ----------
    static int searchMountain(int[] a, int target) {
        int lo = 0, hi = a.length - 1;
        while (lo < hi) { int mid = (lo + hi) >>> 1; if (a[mid] < a[mid + 1]) lo = mid + 1; else hi = mid; }
        int peak = lo;
        int l = 0, r = peak;
        while (l <= r) { int mid = (l + r) >>> 1; if (a[mid] == target) return mid; if (a[mid] < target) l = mid + 1; else r = mid - 1; }
        l = peak + 1; r = a.length - 1;
        while (l <= r) { int mid = (l + r) >>> 1; if (a[mid] == target) return mid; if (a[mid] > target) l = mid + 1; else r = mid - 1; }
        return -1;
    }
}

Pitfalls

  1. Maximize-the-minimum searches the last true: use mid = lo + (hi - lo + 1) / 2.
  2. Real-valued search: iterate a fixed count instead of testing hi - lo > eps.
  3. Check the feasibility function is monotone before building on it.
40 — BACKTRACKING.JAVA

Backtracking

Choose, explore, undo. Subsets and combinations move a START index forward; permutations use a used[] array. For duplicate inputs sort first and skip equal siblings at the same depth. Prune early with a cheap feasibility bound.

PatternUse caseComplexity
Subsets / combinationsStart index moves forwardO(2^n)
Permutationsused[] array, with duplicate skip ruleO(n!)
Constraint searchN-Queens, sudoku with occupancy sets or bitmasksexp
StringsParentheses, partitions, IP addresses, operatorsexp
Backtracking.java
Subsets (+dup), permutations (+unique), combinations, combination sum I/II, parentheses, phone, palindrome partition, word search, N-Queens, sudoku, IP addresses, add operators, gray code
O(2^n) / O(n!) 
import java.util.*;

public class Backtracking {

    // ===== SKELETON =====
    //   void dfs(state) { if (complete) { record; return; } for (choice in choices) { if (!valid) continue; choose; dfs(next); undo; } }
    // Duplicates in input: sort first, then skip `i > start && a[i] == a[i-1]` at the same depth.
    // Subsets vs permutations: subsets move a START index forward; permutations use a USED array.

    // Subsets (LC 78)
    static List<List<Integer>> subsets(int[] a) {
        List<List<Integer>> res = new ArrayList<>();
        subsetsDfs(a, 0, new ArrayList<>(), res);
        return res;
    }

    private static void subsetsDfs(int[] a, int start, List<Integer> cur, List<List<Integer>> res) {
        res.add(new ArrayList<>(cur));
        for (int i = start; i < a.length; i++) {
            cur.add(a[i]);
            subsetsDfs(a, i + 1, cur, res);
            cur.remove(cur.size() - 1);
        }
    }

    // Subsets II with duplicates (LC 90)
    static List<List<Integer>> subsetsWithDup(int[] a) {
        Arrays.sort(a);
        List<List<Integer>> res = new ArrayList<>();
        dupDfs(a, 0, new ArrayList<>(), res);
        return res;
    }

    private static void dupDfs(int[] a, int start, List<Integer> cur, List<List<Integer>> res) {
        res.add(new ArrayList<>(cur));
        for (int i = start; i < a.length; i++) {
            if (i > start && a[i] == a[i - 1]) continue;
            cur.add(a[i]);
            dupDfs(a, i + 1, cur, res);
            cur.remove(cur.size() - 1);
        }
    }

    // Permutations (LC 46)
    static List<List<Integer>> permute(int[] a) {
        List<List<Integer>> res = new ArrayList<>();
        permDfs(a, new boolean[a.length], new ArrayList<>(), res);
        return res;
    }

    private static void permDfs(int[] a, boolean[] used, List<Integer> cur, List<List<Integer>> res) {
        if (cur.size() == a.length) { res.add(new ArrayList<>(cur)); return; }
        for (int i = 0; i < a.length; i++) {
            if (used[i]) continue;
            used[i] = true;
            cur.add(a[i]);
            permDfs(a, used, cur, res);
            cur.remove(cur.size() - 1);
            used[i] = false;
        }
    }

    // Permutations II with duplicates (LC 47): skip a[i] if its equal left twin is not used on this path
    static List<List<Integer>> permuteUnique(int[] a) {
        Arrays.sort(a);
        List<List<Integer>> res = new ArrayList<>();
        uniqDfs(a, new boolean[a.length], new ArrayList<>(), res);
        return res;
    }

    private static void uniqDfs(int[] a, boolean[] used, List<Integer> cur, List<List<Integer>> res) {
        if (cur.size() == a.length) { res.add(new ArrayList<>(cur)); return; }
        for (int i = 0; i < a.length; i++) {
            if (used[i] || (i > 0 && a[i] == a[i - 1] && !used[i - 1])) continue;
            used[i] = true;
            cur.add(a[i]);
            uniqDfs(a, used, cur, res);
            cur.remove(cur.size() - 1);
            used[i] = false;
        }
    }

    // Combinations (LC 77)
    static List<List<Integer>> combine(int n, int k) {
        List<List<Integer>> res = new ArrayList<>();
        combDfs(n, k, 1, new ArrayList<>(), res);
        return res;
    }

    private static void combDfs(int n, int k, int start, List<Integer> cur, List<List<Integer>> res) {
        if (cur.size() == k) { res.add(new ArrayList<>(cur)); return; }
        for (int i = start; i <= n - (k - cur.size()) + 1; i++) { // prune: enough numbers must remain
            cur.add(i);
            combDfs(n, k, i + 1, cur, res);
            cur.remove(cur.size() - 1);
        }
    }

    // Combination Sum (LC 39): reuse allowed -> recurse with the same index
    static List<List<Integer>> combinationSum(int[] c, int target) {
        Arrays.sort(c);
        List<List<Integer>> res = new ArrayList<>();
        csDfs(c, 0, target, new ArrayList<>(), res);
        return res;
    }

    private static void csDfs(int[] c, int start, int remain, List<Integer> cur, List<List<Integer>> res) {
        if (remain == 0) { res.add(new ArrayList<>(cur)); return; }
        for (int i = start; i < c.length && c[i] <= remain; i++) {
            cur.add(c[i]);
            csDfs(c, i, remain - c[i], cur, res);
            cur.remove(cur.size() - 1);
        }
    }

    // Combination Sum II (LC 40): each number once, duplicates present
    static List<List<Integer>> combinationSum2(int[] c, int target) {
        Arrays.sort(c);
        List<List<Integer>> res = new ArrayList<>();
        cs2Dfs(c, 0, target, new ArrayList<>(), res);
        return res;
    }

    private static void cs2Dfs(int[] c, int start, int remain, List<Integer> cur, List<List<Integer>> res) {
        if (remain == 0) { res.add(new ArrayList<>(cur)); return; }
        for (int i = start; i < c.length && c[i] <= remain; i++) {
            if (i > start && c[i] == c[i - 1]) continue;
            cur.add(c[i]);
            cs2Dfs(c, i + 1, remain - c[i], cur, res);
            cur.remove(cur.size() - 1);
        }
    }

    // Generate Parentheses (LC 22): track open / close counts, never let close exceed open
    static List<String> generateParenthesis(int n) {
        List<String> res = new ArrayList<>();
        genDfs(n, 0, 0, new StringBuilder(), res);
        return res;
    }

    private static void genDfs(int n, int open, int close, StringBuilder sb, List<String> res) {
        if (sb.length() == 2 * n) { res.add(sb.toString()); return; }
        if (open < n) { sb.append('('); genDfs(n, open + 1, close, sb, res); sb.setLength(sb.length() - 1); }
        if (close < open) { sb.append(')'); genDfs(n, open, close + 1, sb, res); sb.setLength(sb.length() - 1); }
    }

    // Letter Combinations of a Phone Number (LC 17)
    static List<String> letterCombinations(String digits) {
        List<String> res = new ArrayList<>();
        if (digits.isEmpty()) return res;
        String[] map = {"", "", "abc", "def", "ghi", "jkl", "mno", "pqrs", "tuv", "wxyz"};
        phoneDfs(digits, 0, map, new StringBuilder(), res);
        return res;
    }

    private static void phoneDfs(String d, int i, String[] map, StringBuilder sb, List<String> res) {
        if (i == d.length()) { res.add(sb.toString()); return; }
        for (char c : map[d.charAt(i) - '0'].toCharArray()) {
            sb.append(c);
            phoneDfs(d, i + 1, map, sb, res);
            sb.setLength(sb.length() - 1);
        }
    }

    // Palindrome Partitioning (LC 131)
    static List<List<String>> partition(String s) {
        List<List<String>> res = new ArrayList<>();
        palDfs(s, 0, new ArrayList<>(), res);
        return res;
    }

    private static void palDfs(String s, int start, List<String> cur, List<List<String>> res) {
        if (start == s.length()) { res.add(new ArrayList<>(cur)); return; }
        for (int end = start + 1; end <= s.length(); end++) {
            if (!isPal(s, start, end - 1)) continue;
            cur.add(s.substring(start, end));
            palDfs(s, end, cur, res);
            cur.remove(cur.size() - 1);
        }
    }

    private static boolean isPal(String s, int l, int r) {
        while (l < r) if (s.charAt(l++) != s.charAt(r--)) return false;
        return true;
    }

    // Word Search (LC 79): mark visited in place, restore on the way out
    static boolean exist(char[][] b, String w) {
        for (int i = 0; i < b.length; i++)
            for (int j = 0; j < b[0].length; j++) if (wsDfs(b, w, 0, i, j)) return true;
        return false;
    }

    private static boolean wsDfs(char[][] b, String w, int k, int i, int j) {
        if (k == w.length()) return true;
        if (i < 0 || j < 0 || i >= b.length || j >= b[0].length || b[i][j] != w.charAt(k)) return false;
        char c = b[i][j];
        b[i][j] = '#';
        boolean ok = wsDfs(b, w, k + 1, i + 1, j) || wsDfs(b, w, k + 1, i - 1, j) || wsDfs(b, w, k + 1, i, j + 1) || wsDfs(b, w, k + 1, i, j - 1);
        b[i][j] = c;
        return ok;
    }

    // N-Queens (LC 51): column / diagonal / anti-diagonal occupancy sets -> O(1) validity
    static List<List<String>> solveNQueens(int n) {
        List<List<String>> res = new ArrayList<>();
        queens(n, 0, new int[n], new boolean[n], new boolean[2 * n], new boolean[2 * n], res);
        return res;
    }

    private static void queens(int n, int r, int[] col, boolean[] c, boolean[] d1, boolean[] d2, List<List<String>> res) {
        if (r == n) {
            List<String> board = new ArrayList<>();
            for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
                char[] row = new char[n];
                Arrays.fill(row, '.');
                row[col[i]] = 'Q';
                board.add(new String(row));
            }
            res.add(board);
            return;
        }
        for (int j = 0; j < n; j++) {
            if (c[j] || d1[r + j] || d2[r - j + n]) continue;
            c[j] = d1[r + j] = d2[r - j + n] = true;
            col[r] = j;
            queens(n, r + 1, col, c, d1, d2, res);
            c[j] = d1[r + j] = d2[r - j + n] = false;
        }
    }

    // N-Queens count only, bitmask form (fast)
    static int totalNQueens(int n) { return bits(n, 0, 0, 0, 0); }

    private static int bits(int n, int row, int cols, int d1, int d2) {
        if (row == n) return 1;
        int count = 0, avail = ((1 << n) - 1) & ~(cols | d1 | d2);
        while (avail != 0) {
            int bit = avail & -avail;
            avail ^= bit;
            count += bits(n, row + 1, cols | bit, (d1 | bit) << 1, (d2 | bit) >> 1);
        }
        return count;
    }

    // Sudoku Solver (LC 37): fill the first empty cell, try 1..9 with row/col/box bitmasks
    static boolean solveSudoku(char[][] b) {
        int[] row = new int[9], col = new int[9], box = new int[9];
        for (int i = 0; i < 9; i++)
            for (int j = 0; j < 9; j++)
                if (b[i][j] != '.') {
                    int bit = 1 << (b[i][j] - '1');
                    row[i] |= bit; col[j] |= bit; box[i / 3 * 3 + j / 3] |= bit;
                }
        return sudoku(b, 0, row, col, box);
    }

    private static boolean sudoku(char[][] b, int pos, int[] row, int[] col, int[] box) {
        while (pos < 81 && b[pos / 9][pos % 9] != '.') pos++;
        if (pos == 81) return true;
        int i = pos / 9, j = pos % 9, k = i / 3 * 3 + j / 3;
        for (int d = 0; d < 9; d++) {
            int bit = 1 << d;
            if (((row[i] | col[j] | box[k]) & bit) != 0) continue;
            row[i] |= bit; col[j] |= bit; box[k] |= bit;
            b[i][j] = (char) ('1' + d);
            if (sudoku(b, pos + 1, row, col, box)) return true;
            b[i][j] = '.';
            row[i] ^= bit; col[j] ^= bit; box[k] ^= bit;
        }
        return false;
    }

    // Restore IP Addresses (LC 93)
    static List<String> restoreIpAddresses(String s) {
        List<String> res = new ArrayList<>();
        ipDfs(s, 0, new ArrayList<>(), res);
        return res;
    }

    private static void ipDfs(String s, int i, List<String> parts, List<String> res) {
        if (parts.size() == 4) { if (i == s.length()) res.add(String.join(".", parts)); return; }
        for (int len = 1; len <= 3 && i + len <= s.length(); len++) {
            String p = s.substring(i, i + len);
            if ((p.length() > 1 && p.charAt(0) == '0') || Integer.parseInt(p) > 255) continue;
            parts.add(p);
            ipDfs(s, i + len, parts, res);
            parts.remove(parts.size() - 1);
        }
    }

    // Expression Add Operators (LC 282): carry the last multiplied term so '*' can undo the previous add
    static List<String> addOperators(String num, int target) {
        List<String> res = new ArrayList<>();
        opsDfs(num, target, 0, 0, 0, "", res);
        return res;
    }

    private static void opsDfs(String s, int target, int i, long val, long last, String expr, List<String> res) {
        if (i == s.length()) { if (val == target) res.add(expr); return; }
        for (int j = i; j < s.length(); j++) {
            if (j > i && s.charAt(i) == '0') break;
            long cur = Long.parseLong(s.substring(i, j + 1));
            String t = s.substring(i, j + 1);
            if (i == 0) opsDfs(s, target, j + 1, cur, cur, t, res);
            else {
                opsDfs(s, target, j + 1, val + cur, cur, expr + "+" + t, res);
                opsDfs(s, target, j + 1, val - cur, -cur, expr + "-" + t, res);
                opsDfs(s, target, j + 1, val - last + last * cur, last * cur, expr + "*" + t, res);
            }
        }
    }

    // Gray Code (LC 89): i ^ (i >> 1)
    static List<Integer> grayCode(int n) {
        List<Integer> res = new ArrayList<>();
        for (int i = 0; i < 1 << n; i++) res.add(i ^ (i >> 1));
        return res;
    }
}

Pitfalls

  1. Add a COPY of the current path to the result, not the live list.
  2. Duplicates: i > start && a[i] == a[i-1] for combinations; used[i-1] check for permutations.
  3. Prune before recursing (remaining sum < 0, not enough elements left) instead of after.
41 — BACKTRACKINGVARIANTS.JAVA

Backtracking: Pruning & Structure

Hard backtracking is about cutting the tree: sort and skip symmetric branches, count by symmetry, use BFS when the question is "minimum steps", or skip the search entirely when a formula (factorial number system) picks the answer.

PatternUse caseComplexity
Sort + symmetry skipBucket filling (matchsticks, k subsets)Exponential, pruned
Visit-all pathsUnique paths IIIO(4^cells)
BFS by removalsMinimum removals to be validO(2^n)
No search neededk-th permutation via factorialsO(n^2)
Debt settlingNet balances, backtrack on first non-zeroExponential, pruned
BacktrackingVariants.java
Matchsticks to square, unique paths III, combination sum III, permutation sequence, palindrome permutations, letter case permutation, different ways to add parentheses, remove invalid parentheses, max length of unique-char concatenation, Android unlock patterns, generalized abbreviation, optimal account balancing, all paths in a DAG
Pruned search 
import java.util.*;

public class BacktrackingVariants {

    // ---------- Matchsticks to Square (LC 473): fill 4 sides; sort descending and skip equal-state siblings ----------
    static boolean makesquare(int[] sticks) {
        int sum = 0;
        for (int x : sticks) sum += x;
        if (sum % 4 != 0 || sticks.length < 4) return false;
        Integer[] s = Arrays.stream(sticks).boxed().toArray(Integer[]::new);
        Arrays.sort(s, Collections.reverseOrder());
        return fill(s, 0, new int[4], sum / 4);
    }

    private static boolean fill(Integer[] s, int i, int[] side, int target) {
        if (i == s.length) return true;
        for (int j = 0; j < 4; j++) {
            if (side[j] + s[i] > target) continue;
            boolean dup = false;
            for (int p = 0; p < j; p++) if (side[p] == side[j]) dup = true; // same load as an earlier side: symmetric branch
            if (dup) continue;
            side[j] += s[i];
            if (fill(s, i + 1, side, target)) return true;
            side[j] -= s[i];
        }
        return false;
    }

    // ---------- Unique Paths III (LC 980): visit every empty cell exactly once ----------
    static int uniquePathsIII(int[][] g) {
        int m = g.length, n = g[0].length, empty = 1, sr = 0, sc = 0;
        for (int i = 0; i < m; i++)
            for (int j = 0; j < n; j++) {
                if (g[i][j] == 0) empty++;
                else if (g[i][j] == 1) { sr = i; sc = j; }
            }
        return walk(g, sr, sc, empty);
    }

    private static int walk(int[][] g, int r, int c, int remain) {
        if (r < 0 || c < 0 || r >= g.length || c >= g[0].length || g[r][c] == -1) return 0;
        if (g[r][c] == 2) return remain == 0 ? 1 : 0; // every empty cell and the start were consumed
        int saved = g[r][c];
        g[r][c] = -1;
        int paths = walk(g, r + 1, c, remain - 1) + walk(g, r - 1, c, remain - 1) + walk(g, r, c + 1, remain - 1) + walk(g, r, c - 1, remain - 1);
        g[r][c] = saved;
        return paths;
    }

    // ---------- Combination Sum III (LC 216): k distinct digits 1..9 summing to n ----------
    static List<List<Integer>> combinationSum3(int k, int n) {
        List<List<Integer>> res = new ArrayList<>();
        cs3(k, n, 1, new ArrayList<>(), res);
        return res;
    }

    private static void cs3(int k, int remain, int start, List<Integer> cur, List<List<Integer>> res) {
        if (cur.size() == k) { if (remain == 0) res.add(new ArrayList<>(cur)); return; }
        for (int d = start; d <= 9 && d <= remain; d++) {
            cur.add(d);
            cs3(k, remain - d, d + 1, cur, res);
            cur.remove(cur.size() - 1);
        }
    }

    // ---------- Permutation Sequence (LC 60): no search at all; factorial number system picks each digit directly ----------
    static String getPermutation(int n, int k) {
        List<Integer> digits = new ArrayList<>();
        int[] fact = new int[n + 1];
        fact[0] = 1;
        for (int i = 1; i <= n; i++) { fact[i] = fact[i - 1] * i; digits.add(i); }
        k--;
        StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder();
        for (int i = n; i >= 1; i--) {
            int idx = k / fact[i - 1];
            sb.append(digits.remove(idx));
            k %= fact[i - 1];
        }
        return sb.toString();
    }

    // ---------- Palindrome Permutation II (LC 267): build the left half from half the counts, mirror it ----------
    static List<String> generatePalindromes(String s) {
        int[] cnt = new int[128];
        for (char c : s.toCharArray()) cnt[c]++;
        char mid = 0;
        int odd = 0;
        StringBuilder half = new StringBuilder();
        for (int c = 0; c < 128; c++) {
            if (cnt[c] % 2 == 1) { odd++; mid = (char) c; }
            for (int i = 0; i < cnt[c] / 2; i++) half.append((char) c);
        }
        List<String> res = new ArrayList<>();
        if (odd > 1) return res;
        char[] h = half.toString().toCharArray();
        Arrays.sort(h);
        permuteHalf(h, new boolean[h.length], new StringBuilder(), mid, res);
        return res;
    }

    private static void permuteHalf(char[] h, boolean[] used, StringBuilder cur, char mid, List<String> res) {
        if (cur.length() == h.length) {
            String left = cur.toString();
            res.add(left + (mid == 0 ? "" : String.valueOf(mid)) + new StringBuilder(left).reverse());
            return;
        }
        for (int i = 0; i < h.length; i++) {
            if (used[i] || (i > 0 && h[i] == h[i - 1] && !used[i - 1])) continue;
            used[i] = true;
            cur.append(h[i]);
            permuteHalf(h, used, cur, mid, res);
            cur.setLength(cur.length() - 1);
            used[i] = false;
        }
    }

    // ---------- Letter Case Permutation (LC 784) ----------
    static List<String> letterCasePermutation(String s) {
        List<String> res = new ArrayList<>();
        lcp(s.toCharArray(), 0, res);
        return res;
    }

    private static void lcp(char[] c, int i, List<String> res) {
        if (i == c.length) { res.add(new String(c)); return; }
        lcp(c, i + 1, res);
        if (Character.isLetter(c[i])) {
            c[i] ^= 32; // flip the case bit
            lcp(c, i + 1, res);
            c[i] ^= 32;
        }
    }

    // ---------- Different Ways to Add Parentheses (LC 241): split at every operator, combine left x right results (memoized) ----------
    static List<Integer> diffWaysToCompute(String expr) { return ways(expr, new HashMap<>()); }

    private static List<Integer> ways(String e, Map<String, List<Integer>> memo) {
        if (memo.containsKey(e)) return memo.get(e);
        List<Integer> res = new ArrayList<>();
        for (int i = 0; i < e.length(); i++) {
            char c = e.charAt(i);
            if (c != '+' && c != '-' && c != '*') continue;
            for (int l : ways(e.substring(0, i), memo))
                for (int r : ways(e.substring(i + 1), memo)) res.add(c == '+' ? l + r : c == '-' ? l - r : l * r);
        }
        if (res.isEmpty()) res.add(Integer.parseInt(e));
        memo.put(e, res);
        return res;
    }

    // ---------- Remove Invalid Parentheses (LC 301): BFS by number of removals, first level with a valid string wins ----------
    static List<String> removeInvalidParentheses(String s) {
        List<String> res = new ArrayList<>();
        Set<String> seen = new HashSet<>(List.of(s));
        Deque<String> q = new ArrayDeque<>(List.of(s));
        boolean found = false;
        while (!q.isEmpty() && !found) {
            for (int size = q.size(); size > 0; size--) {
                String cur = q.poll();
                if (validParens(cur)) { res.add(cur); found = true; }
                if (found) continue;
                for (int i = 0; i < cur.length(); i++) {
                    if (cur.charAt(i) != '(' && cur.charAt(i) != ')') continue;
                    String next = cur.substring(0, i) + cur.substring(i + 1);
                    if (seen.add(next)) q.add(next);
                }
            }
        }
        return res;
    }

    private static boolean validParens(String s) {
        int open = 0;
        for (char c : s.toCharArray()) {
            if (c == '(') open++;
            else if (c == ')' && --open < 0) return false;
        }
        return open == 0;
    }

    // ---------- Maximum Length of a Concatenated String with Unique Characters (LC 1239): bitmask per word ----------
    static int maxLength(List<String> arr) {
        List<Integer> masks = new ArrayList<>();
        List<Integer> lens = new ArrayList<>();
        for (String w : arr) {
            int m = 0;
            boolean ok = true;
            for (char c : w.toCharArray()) { if ((m >> (c - 'a') & 1) != 0) { ok = false; break; } m |= 1 << (c - 'a'); }
            if (ok) { masks.add(m); lens.add(w.length()); }
        }
        return pickMax(masks, lens, 0, 0);
    }

    private static int pickMax(List<Integer> masks, List<Integer> lens, int i, int used) {
        if (i == masks.size()) return 0;
        int best = pickMax(masks, lens, i + 1, used);
        if ((masks.get(i) & used) == 0) best = Math.max(best, lens.get(i) + pickMax(masks, lens, i + 1, used | masks.get(i)));
        return best;
    }

    // ---------- Android Unlock Patterns (LC 351): symmetry cuts the search to 3 starts (corner x4, edge x4, center) ----------
    static int numberOfPatterns(int m, int n) {
        int[][] skip = new int[10][10];
        skip[1][3] = skip[3][1] = 2; skip[4][6] = skip[6][4] = 5; skip[7][9] = skip[9][7] = 8;
        skip[1][7] = skip[7][1] = 4; skip[2][8] = skip[8][2] = 5; skip[3][9] = skip[9][3] = 6;
        skip[1][9] = skip[9][1] = skip[3][7] = skip[7][3] = skip[2][8] = skip[8][2] = skip[4][6] = skip[6][4] = 5;
        skip[2][8] = skip[8][2] = 5;
        boolean[] seen = new boolean[10];
        int res = 0;
        for (int len = m; len <= n; len++) {
            res += 4 * dfsPattern(skip, seen, 1, len - 1);
            res += 4 * dfsPattern(skip, seen, 2, len - 1);
            res += dfsPattern(skip, seen, 5, len - 1);
        }
        return res;
    }

    private static int dfsPattern(int[][] skip, boolean[] seen, int cur, int remain) {
        if (remain < 0) return 0;
        if (remain == 0) return 1;
        seen[cur] = true;
        int count = 0;
        for (int next = 1; next <= 9; next++)
            if (!seen[next] && (skip[cur][next] == 0 || seen[skip[cur][next]])) count += dfsPattern(skip, seen, next, remain - 1);
        seen[cur] = false;
        return count;
    }

    // ---------- Generalized Abbreviation (LC 320): each letter is kept or merged into a running count ----------
    static List<String> generateAbbreviations(String word) {
        List<String> res = new ArrayList<>();
        abbr(word, 0, 0, new StringBuilder(), res);
        return res;
    }

    private static void abbr(String w, int i, int run, StringBuilder cur, List<String> res) {
        int len = cur.length();
        if (i == w.length()) {
            if (run > 0) cur.append(run);
            res.add(cur.toString());
        } else {
            abbr(w, i + 1, run + 1, cur, res); // abbreviate this letter
            if (run > 0) cur.append(run);
            cur.append(w.charAt(i));
            abbr(w, i + 1, 0, cur, res);       // keep this letter
        }
        cur.setLength(len);
    }

    // ---------- Optimal Account Balancing (LC 465): net balances, then backtrack settling the first non-zero debt ----------
    static int minTransfers(int[][] transactions) {
        Map<Integer, Integer> net = new HashMap<>();
        for (int[] t : transactions) { net.merge(t[0], -t[2], Integer::sum); net.merge(t[1], t[2], Integer::sum); }
        List<Integer> debts = new ArrayList<>();
        for (int v : net.values()) if (v != 0) debts.add(v);
        return settle(debts, 0);
    }

    private static int settle(List<Integer> d, int i) {
        while (i < d.size() && d.get(i) == 0) i++;
        if (i == d.size()) return 0;
        int best = Integer.MAX_VALUE;
        for (int j = i + 1; j < d.size(); j++) {
            if ((long) d.get(i) * d.get(j) >= 0) continue; // only settle against the opposite sign
            d.set(j, d.get(j) + d.get(i));
            best = Math.min(best, 1 + settle(d, i + 1));
            d.set(j, d.get(j) - d.get(i));
        }
        return best;
    }

    // ---------- All Paths From Source to Target in a DAG (LC 797) ----------
    static List<List<Integer>> allPathsSourceTarget(int[][] graph) {
        List<List<Integer>> res = new ArrayList<>();
        List<Integer> path = new ArrayList<>(List.of(0));
        paths(graph, 0, path, res);
        return res;
    }

    private static void paths(int[][] g, int u, List<Integer> path, List<List<Integer>> res) {
        if (u == g.length - 1) { res.add(new ArrayList<>(path)); return; }
        for (int v : g[u]) {
            path.add(v);
            paths(g, v, path, res);
            path.remove(path.size() - 1);
        }
    }
}

Pitfalls

  1. Equal-state siblings explore the same subtree: skip a bucket with the same load as an earlier one.
  2. Undo exactly what you did (restore cells, pop path entries, reset lengths).
  3. If the question asks for the k-th item, do not enumerate.

Greedy

Greedy is right when an exchange argument or a "stays ahead" invariant holds. State the argument in one sentence before coding; if you cannot, think DP. Typical shapes: furthest reach, sort by a key, two passes, ratio ordering, heap of options.

PatternUse caseComplexity
Reach / jumpsTrack the furthest frontierO(n)
Two-passCandy, gas station style prefix logicO(n)
Sort then sweepAssign cookies, boats, largest numberO(n log n)
Greedy + heapRefueling stops, scheduling with choicesO(n log n)
Greedy.java
Jump game I/II, gas station, candy, partition labels, queue reconstruction, cookies, largest number, units, valid parenthesis string, boats, refueling, straights, lemonade
O(n log n) 
import java.util.*;

public class Greedy {

    // PROOF HABIT: greedy works when an exchange argument holds (swap the optimal's choice for yours without loss)
    // or when a "stays ahead" invariant holds. If you cannot argue it in one sentence, think DP.

    // Jump Game (LC 55): furthest reachable
    static boolean canJump(int[] a) {
        int far = 0;
        for (int i = 0; i < a.length; i++) {
            if (i > far) return false;
            far = Math.max(far, i + a[i]);
        }
        return true;
    }

    // Jump Game II (LC 45): BFS levels implicitly -- extend the frontier when the current one is exhausted
    static int jump(int[] a) {
        int jumps = 0, curEnd = 0, far = 0;
        for (int i = 0; i < a.length - 1; i++) {
            far = Math.max(far, i + a[i]);
            if (i == curEnd) { jumps++; curEnd = far; }
        }
        return jumps;
    }

    // Gas Station (LC 134): if total >= 0 a start exists; restart after any prefix that goes negative
    static int canCompleteCircuit(int[] gas, int[] cost) {
        int total = 0, tank = 0, start = 0;
        for (int i = 0; i < gas.length; i++) {
            int d = gas[i] - cost[i];
            total += d;
            tank += d;
            if (tank < 0) { start = i + 1; tank = 0; }
        }
        return total >= 0 ? start : -1;
    }

    // Candy (LC 135): left pass, right pass
    static int candy(int[] r) {
        int n = r.length;
        int[] c = new int[n];
        Arrays.fill(c, 1);
        for (int i = 1; i < n; i++) if (r[i] > r[i - 1]) c[i] = c[i - 1] + 1;
        for (int i = n - 2; i >= 0; i--) if (r[i] > r[i + 1]) c[i] = Math.max(c[i], c[i + 1] + 1);
        int sum = 0;
        for (int x : c) sum += x;
        return sum;
    }

    // Partition Labels (LC 763): extend to the last occurrence
    static List<Integer> partitionLabels(String s) {
        int[] last = new int[26];
        for (int i = 0; i < s.length(); i++) last[s.charAt(i) - 'a'] = i;
        List<Integer> res = new ArrayList<>();
        int start = 0, end = 0;
        for (int i = 0; i < s.length(); i++) {
            end = Math.max(end, last[s.charAt(i) - 'a']);
            if (i == end) { res.add(end - start + 1); start = i + 1; }
        }
        return res;
    }

    // Queue Reconstruction by Height (LC 406): tallest first, insert at index k
    static int[][] reconstructQueue(int[][] people) {
        Arrays.sort(people, (a, b) -> a[0] != b[0] ? b[0] - a[0] : a[1] - b[1]);
        List<int[]> out = new ArrayList<>();
        for (int[] p : people) out.add(p[1], p);
        return out.toArray(new int[0][]);
    }

    // Assign Cookies (LC 455): smallest cookie that satisfies the least greedy child
    static int findContentChildren(int[] g, int[] s) {
        Arrays.sort(g);
        Arrays.sort(s);
        int i = 0;
        for (int j = 0; j < s.length && i < g.length; j++) if (s[j] >= g[i]) i++;
        return i;
    }

    // Largest Number (LC 179): comparator a+b vs b+a
    static String largestNumber(int[] a) {
        String[] s = new String[a.length];
        for (int i = 0; i < a.length; i++) s[i] = String.valueOf(a[i]);
        Arrays.sort(s, (x, y) -> (y + x).compareTo(x + y));
        if (s[0].equals("0")) return "0";
        return String.join("", s);
    }

    // Task order minimizing lateness / weighted completion: sort by ratio (exchange argument)
    // Example: Minimum Cost to Hire Workers style ratios live in HeapsTopK; here: Maximum units on a truck (LC 1710)
    static int maximumUnits(int[][] boxes, int truckSize) {
        Arrays.sort(boxes, (a, b) -> b[1] - a[1]);
        int units = 0;
        for (int[] b : boxes) {
            int take = Math.min(b[0], truckSize);
            units += take * b[1];
            truckSize -= take;
            if (truckSize == 0) break;
        }
        return units;
    }

    // Valid Parenthesis String (LC 678): track the range [lo, hi] of possible open counts
    static boolean checkValidString(String s) {
        int lo = 0, hi = 0;
        for (char c : s.toCharArray()) {
            lo += c == '(' ? 1 : -1;
            hi += c == ')' ? -1 : 1;
            if (hi < 0) return false;
            lo = Math.max(lo, 0);
        }
        return lo == 0;
    }

    // Boats to Save People (LC 881): pair heaviest with lightest
    static int numRescueBoats(int[] p, int limit) {
        Arrays.sort(p);
        int i = 0, j = p.length - 1, boats = 0;
        while (i <= j) { if (p[i] + p[j] <= limit) i++; j--; boats++; }
        return boats;
    }

    // Minimum Number of Refueling Stops (LC 871): greedy with a max-heap of passed stations
    static int minRefuelStops(int target, int startFuel, int[][] stations) {
        PriorityQueue<Integer> pq = new PriorityQueue<>(Collections.reverseOrder());
        long fuel = startFuel;
        int stops = 0, i = 0;
        while (fuel < target) {
            while (i < stations.length && stations[i][0] <= fuel) pq.add(stations[i++][1]);
            if (pq.isEmpty()) return -1;
            fuel += pq.poll();
            stops++;
        }
        return stops;
    }

    // Hand of Straights (LC 846): always start from the smallest remaining card
    static boolean isNStraightHand(int[] hand, int w) {
        if (hand.length % w != 0) return false;
        TreeMap<Integer, Integer> cnt = new TreeMap<>();
        for (int h : hand) cnt.merge(h, 1, Integer::sum);
        while (!cnt.isEmpty()) {
            int first = cnt.firstKey();
            for (int c = first; c < first + w; c++) {
                Integer v = cnt.get(c);
                if (v == null) return false;
                if (v == 1) cnt.remove(c); else cnt.put(c, v - 1);
            }
        }
        return true;
    }

    // Lemonade Change (LC 860)
    static boolean lemonadeChange(int[] bills) {
        int five = 0, ten = 0;
        for (int b : bills) {
            if (b == 5) five++;
            else if (b == 10) { if (five == 0) return false; five--; ten++; }
            else {
                if (ten > 0 && five > 0) { ten--; five--; }
                else if (five >= 3) five -= 3;
                else return false;
            }
        }
        return true;
    }
}

Pitfalls

  1. Without a proof sketch, test the greedy against brute force on small inputs.
  2. Largest Number: compare a+b with b+a, and special-case an all-zero result.
  3. Valid Parenthesis String: carry a range [lo, hi] of possible open counts, not a single count.
43 — GREEDYVARIANTS.JAVA

Greedy: Exchange & Construction

Most hard greedy problems are one of: sort by a derived key, construct digit by digit, repair a violation locally, or work backwards. If you cannot state the exchange argument, prove it on a tiny case first.

PatternUse caseComplexity
Sort by derived keyDifference, ratio, end timeO(n log n)
Monotone stack constructionLexicographically smallest subsequenceO(n)
Work backwardsOperations that are easier to undo than to doO(log n)
Digit constructionLargest number by one swap / mergeO(n)
Local repairMake array non-decreasing with one changeO(n)
GreedyVariants.java
Remove duplicate letters, wiggle subsequence, two-city scheduling, bag of tokens, broken calculator, monotone increasing digits, split array into consecutive subsequences, maximum swap, non-decreasing array, advantage shuffle, fractional knapsack, domino rotations, create maximum number, min add to make valid, min operations to form a target, longest pair chain
Hard variants 
import java.util.*;

public class GreedyVariants {

    // Each entry: the greedy choice, then WHY it is safe (the exchange argument in one line).

    // Maximize Sum After K Negations (LC 1005): always flip the current smallest value (a negative if any remains)
    static int largestSumAfterKNegations(int[] a, int k) {
        PriorityQueue<Integer> pq = new PriorityQueue<>();
        for (int x : a) pq.add(x);
        while (k-- > 0) pq.add(-pq.poll());
        int sum = 0;
        for (int x : pq) sum += x;
        return sum;
    }

    // Wiggle Subsequence (LC 376): count direction changes (a peak or valley is always worth keeping)
    static int wiggleMaxLength(int[] a) {
        if (a.length < 2) return a.length;
        int up = 1, down = 1;
        for (int i = 1; i < a.length; i++) {
            if (a[i] > a[i - 1]) up = down + 1;
            else if (a[i] < a[i - 1]) down = up + 1;
        }
        return Math.max(up, down);
    }

    // Remove Duplicate Letters / Smallest Subsequence of Distinct Characters (LC 316 / 1081)
    // Pop a bigger letter off the stack only if it appears again later; skip letters already on the stack.
    static String removeDuplicateLetters(String s) {
        int[] last = new int[26];
        for (int i = 0; i < s.length(); i++) last[s.charAt(i) - 'a'] = i;
        boolean[] in = new boolean[26];
        StringBuilder st = new StringBuilder();
        for (int i = 0; i < s.length(); i++) {
            char c = s.charAt(i);
            if (in[c - 'a']) continue;
            while (st.length() > 0 && st.charAt(st.length() - 1) > c && last[st.charAt(st.length() - 1) - 'a'] > i) {
                in[st.charAt(st.length() - 1) - 'a'] = false;
                st.setLength(st.length() - 1);
            }
            st.append(c);
            in[c - 'a'] = true;
        }
        return st.toString();
    }

    // Two City Scheduling (LC 1029): send everyone to A, then move the n people with the smallest (costB - costA)
    static int twoCitySchedCost(int[][] costs) {
        Arrays.sort(costs, (x, y) -> (x[1] - x[0]) - (y[1] - y[0]));
        int n = costs.length / 2, total = 0;
        for (int i = 0; i < costs.length; i++) total += i < n ? costs[i][1] : costs[i][0];
        return total;
    }

    // Bag of Tokens (LC 948): spend power on the cheapest token, gain it back by selling the dearest
    static int bagOfTokensScore(int[] tokens, int power) {
        Arrays.sort(tokens);
        int l = 0, r = tokens.length - 1, score = 0, best = 0;
        while (l <= r) {
            if (power >= tokens[l]) { power -= tokens[l++]; best = Math.max(best, ++score); }
            else if (score > 0) { power += tokens[r--]; score--; }
            else break;
        }
        return best;
    }

    // Broken Calculator (LC 991): go BACKWARD from target: halve if even, else add one
    static int brokenCalc(int start, int target) {
        int ops = 0;
        while (target > start) { target = target % 2 == 0 ? target / 2 : target + 1; ops++; }
        return ops + start - target;
    }

    // Monotone Increasing Digits (LC 738): find the first drop, decrement it, fill the rest with 9s
    static int monotoneIncreasingDigits(int n) {
        char[] d = String.valueOf(n).toCharArray();
        int mark = d.length;
        for (int i = d.length - 1; i > 0; i--) if (d[i - 1] > d[i]) { d[i - 1]--; mark = i; }
        for (int i = mark; i < d.length; i++) d[i] = '9';
        return Integer.parseInt(new String(d));
    }

    // Split Array into Consecutive Subsequences (LC 659): append to an existing run if possible, else start a new run of 3
    static boolean isPossibleSplit(int[] nums) {
        Map<Integer, Integer> count = new HashMap<>(), tail = new HashMap<>();
        for (int x : nums) count.merge(x, 1, Integer::sum);
        for (int x : nums) {
            if (count.get(x) == 0) continue;
            count.merge(x, -1, Integer::sum);
            if (tail.getOrDefault(x - 1, 0) > 0) { // extend a run ending at x - 1
                tail.merge(x - 1, -1, Integer::sum);
                tail.merge(x, 1, Integer::sum);
            } else if (count.getOrDefault(x + 1, 0) > 0 && count.getOrDefault(x + 2, 0) > 0) {
                count.merge(x + 1, -1, Integer::sum);
                count.merge(x + 2, -1, Integer::sum);
                tail.merge(x + 2, 1, Integer::sum);
            } else return false;
        }
        return true;
    }

    // Maximum Swap (LC 670): swap the first digit that has a larger digit to its right with the LAST occurrence of that larger digit
    static int maximumSwap(int num) {
        char[] d = String.valueOf(num).toCharArray();
        int[] last = new int[10];
        for (int i = 0; i < d.length; i++) last[d[i] - '0'] = i;
        for (int i = 0; i < d.length; i++)
            for (int v = 9; v > d[i] - '0'; v--)
                if (last[v] > i) {
                    char t = d[i]; d[i] = d[last[v]]; d[last[v]] = t;
                    return Integer.parseInt(new String(d));
                }
        return num;
    }

    // Non-decreasing Array with at most one change (LC 665): on a drop prefer lowering a[i - 1]; else raise a[i]
    static boolean checkPossibility(int[] a) {
        int[] b = a.clone();
        int changes = 0;
        for (int i = 1; i < b.length; i++) {
            if (b[i - 1] <= b[i]) continue;
            if (++changes > 1) return false;
            if (i < 2 || b[i - 2] <= b[i]) b[i - 1] = b[i]; else b[i] = b[i - 1];
        }
        return true;
    }

    // Advantage Shuffle (LC 870): beat each of B with the smallest A that wins; throw leftovers at what cannot be beaten
    static int[] advantageCount(int[] a, int[] b) {
        int n = a.length;
        int[] sa = a.clone();
        Arrays.sort(sa);
        Integer[] idx = new Integer[n];
        for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) idx[i] = i;
        Arrays.sort(idx, (x, y) -> b[x] - b[y]);
        int[] res = new int[n];
        int lo = 0, hi = n - 1;
        for (int i = n - 1; i >= 0; i--) { // largest B first: use the largest A if it wins, else sacrifice the smallest A
            int bi = idx[i];
            if (sa[hi] > b[bi]) res[bi] = sa[hi--]; else res[bi] = sa[lo++];
        }
        return res;
    }

    // Fractional Knapsack: sort by value / weight (the only knapsack where greedy is optimal)
    static double fractionalKnapsack(int[] wt, int[] val, int cap) {
        int n = wt.length;
        Integer[] idx = new Integer[n];
        for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) idx[i] = i;
        Arrays.sort(idx, (x, y) -> Double.compare((double) val[y] / wt[y], (double) val[x] / wt[x]));
        double total = 0;
        for (int i : idx) {
            int take = Math.min(wt[i], cap);
            total += (double) val[i] * take / wt[i];
            cap -= take;
            if (cap == 0) break;
        }
        return total;
    }

    // Minimum Domino Rotations (LC 1007): only tops[0] or bottoms[0] can be the final value
    static int minDominoRotations(int[] tops, int[] bottoms) {
        int best = Math.min(rotations(tops, bottoms, tops[0]), rotations(tops, bottoms, bottoms[0]));
        return best == Integer.MAX_VALUE ? -1 : best;
    }

    private static int rotations(int[] t, int[] b, int target) {
        int topSwaps = 0, botSwaps = 0;
        for (int i = 0; i < t.length; i++) {
            if (t[i] != target && b[i] != target) return Integer.MAX_VALUE;
            if (t[i] != target) topSwaps++;
            if (b[i] != target) botSwaps++;
        }
        return Math.min(topSwaps, botSwaps);
    }

    // Create Maximum Number (LC 321): best i digits of a + best k-i of b, merge by lexicographic suffix comparison
    static int[] maxNumber(int[] a, int[] b, int k) {
        int[] best = new int[k];
        for (int i = Math.max(0, k - b.length); i <= Math.min(k, a.length); i++) {
            int[] cand = merge(pick(a, i), pick(b, k - i));
            if (greater(cand, 0, best, 0)) best = cand;
        }
        return best;
    }

    private static int[] pick(int[] a, int k) { // largest subsequence of length k
        int[] st = new int[k];
        int top = 0, drop = a.length - k;
        for (int x : a) {
            while (drop > 0 && top > 0 && st[top - 1] < x) { top--; drop--; }
            if (top < k) st[top++] = x; else drop--;
        }
        return st;
    }

    private static int[] merge(int[] a, int[] b) {
        int[] res = new int[a.length + b.length];
        int i = 0, j = 0;
        for (int r = 0; r < res.length; r++) res[r] = greater(a, i, b, j) ? a[i++] : b[j++];
        return res;
    }

    private static boolean greater(int[] a, int i, int[] b, int j) { // is suffix a[i..] lexicographically > b[j..]?
        while (i < a.length && j < b.length && a[i] == b[j]) { i++; j++; }
        return j == b.length || (i < a.length && a[i] > b[j]);
    }

    // Minimum Add to Make Parentheses Valid (LC 921)
    static int minAddToMakeValid(String s) {
        int open = 0, add = 0;
        for (char c : s.toCharArray()) {
            if (c == '(') open++; else if (open > 0) open--; else add++;
        }
        return add + open;
    }

    // Minimum Number of Increments on Subarrays to Form Target (LC 1526): sum of positive steps up
    static int minNumberOperations(int[] target) {
        int ops = target[0];
        for (int i = 1; i < target.length; i++) ops += Math.max(0, target[i] - target[i - 1]);
        return ops;
    }

    // Maximum Length of Pair Chain (LC 646): sort by END, take whenever compatible
    static int findLongestChain(int[][] pairs) {
        Arrays.sort(pairs, (x, y) -> x[1] - y[1]);
        int count = 0;
        long end = Long.MIN_VALUE;
        for (int[] p : pairs) if (p[0] > end) { count++; end = p[1]; }
        return count;
    }
}

Pitfalls

  1. Greedy without a proof fails on a counterexample; test the rule on 3-4 element inputs.
  2. Work-backwards problems: divide or subtract from the target instead of multiplying from the start.
  3. Sort stability and ties matter when the derived key can be equal.
44 — LINKEDLISTS.JAVA

Linked Lists

Use a dummy head whenever the head can change. Slow/fast pointers find the middle and the cycle; reversing the second half turns many problems (palindrome, reorder) into a merge of two lists. Draw the pointers before coding.

PatternUse caseComplexity
ReverseWhole list, a range, k-groupsO(n)
Slow / fastMiddle, cycle entry, nth from endO(n)
MergeTwo lists, K lists by divide and conquer, sort listO(n log n)
Pointer surgeryReorder, partition, rotate, copy with random pointerO(n)
LinkedLists.java
Reverse (range, k-group), swap pairs, middle, cycle, remove nth, merge, merge K, sort, reorder, palindrome, add numbers, intersection, dedupe II, partition, rotate, odd-even, copy random
O(n) 
import java.util.*;

public class LinkedLists {

    static class ListNode {
        int val;
        ListNode next;
        ListNode(int v) { val = v; }
    }

    // Test helpers
    static ListNode of(int... a) {
        ListNode dummy = new ListNode(0), t = dummy;
        for (int x : a) { t.next = new ListNode(x); t = t.next; }
        return dummy.next;
    }

    static String str(ListNode n) {
        StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder("[");
        for (; n != null; n = n.next) sb.append(n.val).append(n.next != null ? "," : "");
        return sb.append("]").toString();
    }

    // DUMMY HEAD: use it whenever the head itself might change (delete, merge, partition, reverse range).

    // Reverse (LC 206): iterative
    static ListNode reverse(ListNode head) {
        ListNode prev = null;
        while (head != null) { ListNode nx = head.next; head.next = prev; prev = head; head = nx; }
        return prev;
    }

    // Reverse Between (LC 92)
    static ListNode reverseBetween(ListNode head, int left, int right) {
        ListNode dummy = new ListNode(0);
        dummy.next = head;
        ListNode pre = dummy;
        for (int i = 1; i < left; i++) pre = pre.next;
        ListNode cur = pre.next;
        for (int i = 0; i < right - left; i++) { // pull the next node to the front of the segment
            ListNode nx = cur.next;
            cur.next = nx.next;
            nx.next = pre.next;
            pre.next = nx;
        }
        return dummy.next;
    }

    // Reverse Nodes in k-Group (LC 25)
    static ListNode reverseKGroup(ListNode head, int k) {
        ListNode probe = head;
        for (int i = 0; i < k; i++) { if (probe == null) return head; probe = probe.next; }
        ListNode prev = reverseKGroup(probe, k), cur = head;
        for (int i = 0; i < k; i++) { ListNode nx = cur.next; cur.next = prev; prev = cur; cur = nx; }
        return prev;
    }

    // Swap Nodes in Pairs (LC 24)
    static ListNode swapPairs(ListNode head) {
        ListNode dummy = new ListNode(0), prev = dummy;
        dummy.next = head;
        while (prev.next != null && prev.next.next != null) {
            ListNode a = prev.next, b = a.next;
            a.next = b.next;
            b.next = a;
            prev.next = b;
            prev = a;
        }
        return dummy.next;
    }

    // Middle (LC 876): slow / fast; for even length returns the second middle
    static ListNode middle(ListNode head) {
        ListNode s = head, f = head;
        while (f != null && f.next != null) { s = s.next; f = f.next.next; }
        return s;
    }

    // Cycle detection + entry (LC 141 / 142): Floyd
    static ListNode detectCycle(ListNode head) {
        ListNode s = head, f = head;
        while (f != null && f.next != null) {
            s = s.next;
            f = f.next.next;
            if (s == f) {
                s = head;
                while (s != f) { s = s.next; f = f.next; }
                return s;
            }
        }
        return null;
    }

    // Remove Nth From End (LC 19): gap of n between two pointers
    static ListNode removeNthFromEnd(ListNode head, int n) {
        ListNode dummy = new ListNode(0), fast = dummy, slow = dummy;
        dummy.next = head;
        for (int i = 0; i <= n; i++) fast = fast.next;
        while (fast != null) { fast = fast.next; slow = slow.next; }
        slow.next = slow.next.next;
        return dummy.next;
    }

    // Merge Two Sorted Lists (LC 21)
    static ListNode mergeTwo(ListNode a, ListNode b) {
        ListNode dummy = new ListNode(0), t = dummy;
        while (a != null && b != null) {
            if (a.val <= b.val) { t.next = a; a = a.next; } else { t.next = b; b = b.next; }
            t = t.next;
        }
        t.next = a != null ? a : b;
        return dummy.next;
    }

    // Merge K Lists (LC 23): divide and conquer, O(N log k), no heap needed
    static ListNode mergeKLists(ListNode[] lists) {
        if (lists.length == 0) return null;
        for (int step = 1; step < lists.length; step *= 2)
            for (int i = 0; i + step < lists.length; i += 2 * step) lists[i] = mergeTwo(lists[i], lists[i + step]);
        return lists[0];
    }

    // Sort List (LC 148): merge sort, split with slow/fast
    static ListNode sortList(ListNode head) {
        if (head == null || head.next == null) return head;
        ListNode slow = head, fast = head.next;
        while (fast != null && fast.next != null) { slow = slow.next; fast = fast.next.next; }
        ListNode right = slow.next;
        slow.next = null;
        return mergeTwo(sortList(head), sortList(right));
    }

    // Reorder List (LC 143): middle -> reverse second half -> interleave
    static void reorderList(ListNode head) {
        if (head == null || head.next == null) return;
        ListNode mid = middle(head), second = reverse(mid.next);
        mid.next = null;
        ListNode first = head;
        while (second != null) {
            ListNode a = first.next, b = second.next;
            first.next = second;
            second.next = a;
            first = a;
            second = b;
        }
    }

    // Palindrome List (LC 234)
    static boolean isPalindrome(ListNode head) {
        ListNode mid = middle(head), second = reverse(mid), first = head;
        while (second != null) {
            if (first.val != second.val) return false;
            first = first.next;
            second = second.next;
        }
        return true;
    }

    // Add Two Numbers (LC 2): digits in reverse order
    static ListNode addTwoNumbers(ListNode a, ListNode b) {
        ListNode dummy = new ListNode(0), t = dummy;
        int carry = 0;
        while (a != null || b != null || carry > 0) {
            int s = carry + (a != null ? a.val : 0) + (b != null ? b.val : 0);
            t.next = new ListNode(s % 10);
            carry = s / 10;
            t = t.next;
            if (a != null) a = a.next;
            if (b != null) b = b.next;
        }
        return dummy.next;
    }

    // Intersection of Two Lists (LC 160): switch heads at the end, meet at the intersection (or both null)
    static ListNode getIntersectionNode(ListNode a, ListNode b) {
        ListNode p = a, q = b;
        while (p != q) {
            p = p == null ? b : p.next;
            q = q == null ? a : q.next;
        }
        return p;
    }

    // Remove Duplicates from Sorted List II (LC 82): drop every value that repeats
    static ListNode deleteDuplicates(ListNode head) {
        ListNode dummy = new ListNode(0), prev = dummy;
        dummy.next = head;
        while (head != null) {
            if (head.next != null && head.val == head.next.val) {
                while (head.next != null && head.val == head.next.val) head = head.next;
                prev.next = head.next;
            } else prev = prev.next;
            head = head.next;
        }
        return dummy.next;
    }

    // Partition List (LC 86): two dummy lists
    static ListNode partition(ListNode head, int x) {
        ListNode lo = new ListNode(0), hi = new ListNode(0), a = lo, b = hi;
        for (; head != null; head = head.next) {
            if (head.val < x) { a.next = head; a = a.next; } else { b.next = head; b = b.next; }
        }
        b.next = null;
        a.next = hi.next;
        return lo.next;
    }

    // Rotate List (LC 61)
    static ListNode rotateRight(ListNode head, int k) {
        if (head == null || head.next == null || k == 0) return head;
        int n = 1;
        ListNode tail = head;
        while (tail.next != null) { tail = tail.next; n++; }
        k %= n;
        if (k == 0) return head;
        ListNode newTail = head;
        for (int i = 0; i < n - k - 1; i++) newTail = newTail.next;
        ListNode newHead = newTail.next;
        newTail.next = null;
        tail.next = head;
        return newHead;
    }

    // Odd Even Linked List (LC 328)
    static ListNode oddEvenList(ListNode head) {
        if (head == null) return null;
        ListNode odd = head, even = head.next, evenHead = even;
        while (even != null && even.next != null) {
            odd.next = even.next;
            odd = odd.next;
            even.next = odd.next;
            even = even.next;
        }
        odd.next = evenHead;
        return head;
    }

    // Copy List with Random Pointer (LC 138): interleave copies, set randoms, split. O(1) extra space.
    static class RNode {
        int val;
        RNode next, random;
        RNode(int v) { val = v; }
    }

    static RNode copyRandomList(RNode head) {
        if (head == null) return null;
        for (RNode c = head; c != null; c = c.next.next) {
            RNode cp = new RNode(c.val);
            cp.next = c.next;
            c.next = cp;
        }
        for (RNode c = head; c != null; c = c.next.next) if (c.random != null) c.next.random = c.random.next;
        RNode newHead = head.next;
        for (RNode c = head; c != null; c = c.next) {
            RNode cp = c.next;
            c.next = cp.next;
            if (cp.next != null) cp.next = cp.next.next;
        }
        return newHead;
    }
}

Pitfalls

  1. Dummy head removes every "is it the head?" special case.
  2. Save next BEFORE overwriting it when reversing.
  3. Cycle entry: after slow meets fast, restart one pointer at the head and move both one step.

Linked Lists: Pointer Surgery

More pointer surgery: prefix-sum tricks, in-place arithmetic on digit lists, conditional group reversal, circular and multilevel lists. Draw the pointers before coding.

PatternUse caseComplexity
Prefix sum mapRemove zero-sum runsO(n)
Gap pointersKth from the end, swap nodesO(n)
Count then reverseReverse groups only if even lengthO(n)
Stack of next pointersFlatten multilevel listsO(n)

LinkedListsVariants.java
Remove zero-sum sublists, next larger node, split list in parts, plus one, swap nodes, delete middle, twin sum, merge between zeros, merge in between, reverse even-length groups, insertion sort list, binary to decimal, remove elements, insert into circular list, cycle length, flatten multilevel doubly linked list
Pointer surgery 
import java.util.*;

public class LinkedListsVariants {
    // Reuses LinkedLists.ListNode, LinkedLists.of and LinkedLists.str.
    // Rule of thumb: dummy head when the head can change; two pointers (gap or fast/slow) when a length is needed; stack when "next greater".

    // ---------- Remove Zero Sum Consecutive Nodes (LC 1171): equal prefix sums bracket a zero-sum run ----------
    static LinkedLists.ListNode removeZeroSumSublists(LinkedLists.ListNode head) {
        LinkedLists.ListNode dummy = new LinkedLists.ListNode(0);
        dummy.next = head;
        Map<Integer, LinkedLists.ListNode> seen = new HashMap<>();
        int prefix = 0;
        for (LinkedLists.ListNode n = dummy; n != null; n = n.next) { // pass 1: remember the LAST node for each prefix sum
            prefix += n.val;
            seen.put(prefix, n);
        }
        prefix = 0;
        for (LinkedLists.ListNode n = dummy; n != null; n = n.next) { // pass 2: jump over everything up to that last node
            prefix += n.val;
            n.next = seen.get(prefix).next;
        }
        return dummy.next;
    }

    // ---------- Next Greater Node in Linked List (LC 1019): copy to an array, monotone stack ----------
    static int[] nextLargerNodes(LinkedLists.ListNode head) {
        List<Integer> vals = new ArrayList<>();
        for (LinkedLists.ListNode n = head; n != null; n = n.next) vals.add(n.val);
        int[] res = new int[vals.size()];
        Deque<Integer> st = new ArrayDeque<>();
        for (int i = 0; i < res.length; i++) {
            while (!st.isEmpty() && vals.get(st.peek()) < vals.get(i)) res[st.pop()] = vals.get(i);
            st.push(i);
        }
        return res;
    }

    // ---------- Split Linked List in Parts (LC 725): sizes differ by at most one, earlier parts larger ----------
    static LinkedLists.ListNode[] splitListToParts(LinkedLists.ListNode head, int k) {
        int n = 0;
        for (LinkedLists.ListNode c = head; c != null; c = c.next) n++;
        LinkedLists.ListNode[] parts = new LinkedLists.ListNode[k];
        LinkedLists.ListNode cur = head;
        for (int i = 0; i < k; i++) {
            int size = n / k + (i < n % k ? 1 : 0);
            parts[i] = cur;
            for (int j = 0; j < size - 1 && cur != null; j++) cur = cur.next;
            if (cur != null) { LinkedLists.ListNode nx = cur.next; cur.next = null; cur = nx; }
        }
        return parts;
    }

    // ---------- Plus One Linked List (LC 369): rightmost non-9 node gets +1, everything after becomes 0 ----------
    static LinkedLists.ListNode plusOne(LinkedLists.ListNode head) {
        LinkedLists.ListNode dummy = new LinkedLists.ListNode(0), notNine = dummy;
        dummy.next = head;
        for (LinkedLists.ListNode n = head; n != null; n = n.next) if (n.val != 9) notNine = n;
        notNine.val++;
        for (LinkedLists.ListNode n = notNine.next; n != null; n = n.next) n.val = 0;
        return dummy.val == 0 ? head : dummy;
    }

    // ---------- Swapping Nodes in a Linked List (LC 1721): kth from the start and kth from the end, swap values ----------
    static LinkedLists.ListNode swapNodes(LinkedLists.ListNode head, int k) {
        LinkedLists.ListNode first = head;
        for (int i = 1; i < k; i++) first = first.next;
        LinkedLists.ListNode second = head, fast = first;
        while (fast.next != null) { fast = fast.next; second = second.next; } // gap of k - 1 puts `second` kth from the end
        int t = first.val; first.val = second.val; second.val = t;
        return head;
    }

    // ---------- Delete the Middle Node (LC 2095): slow stops one before the middle if fast starts two ahead ----------
    static LinkedLists.ListNode deleteMiddle(LinkedLists.ListNode head) {
        if (head.next == null) return null;
        LinkedLists.ListNode slow = head, fast = head.next.next;
        while (fast != null && fast.next != null) { slow = slow.next; fast = fast.next.next; }
        slow.next = slow.next.next;
        return head;
    }

    // ---------- Maximum Twin Sum (LC 2130): reverse the second half, then walk both halves ----------
    static int pairSum(LinkedLists.ListNode head) {
        LinkedLists.ListNode slow = head, fast = head;
        while (fast != null && fast.next != null) { slow = slow.next; fast = fast.next.next; }
        LinkedLists.ListNode prev = null;
        while (slow != null) { LinkedLists.ListNode nx = slow.next; slow.next = prev; prev = slow; slow = nx; }
        int best = 0;
        for (LinkedLists.ListNode a = head, b = prev; b != null; a = a.next, b = b.next) best = Math.max(best, a.val + b.val);
        return best;
    }

    // ---------- Merge Nodes in Between Zeros (LC 2181) ----------
    static LinkedLists.ListNode mergeNodes(LinkedLists.ListNode head) {
        LinkedLists.ListNode dummy = new LinkedLists.ListNode(0), tail = dummy;
        int sum = 0;
        for (LinkedLists.ListNode n = head.next; n != null; n = n.next) {
            if (n.val == 0) { tail.next = new LinkedLists.ListNode(sum); tail = tail.next; sum = 0; }
            else sum += n.val;
        }
        return dummy.next;
    }

    // ---------- Merge In Between Linked Lists (LC 1669): replace nodes a..b of list1 with all of list2 ----------
    static LinkedLists.ListNode mergeInBetween(LinkedLists.ListNode list1, int a, int b, LinkedLists.ListNode list2) {
        LinkedLists.ListNode before = list1;
        for (int i = 0; i < a - 1; i++) before = before.next;
        LinkedLists.ListNode after = before;
        for (int i = 0; i < b - a + 2; i++) after = after.next;
        before.next = list2;
        LinkedLists.ListNode tail = list2;
        while (tail.next != null) tail = tail.next;
        tail.next = after;
        return list1;
    }

    // ---------- Reverse Nodes in Even Length Groups (LC 2074): group sizes 1, 2, 3, ...; reverse a group if its real size is even ----------
    static LinkedLists.ListNode reverseEvenLengthGroups(LinkedLists.ListNode head) {
        LinkedLists.ListNode dummy = new LinkedLists.ListNode(0), prev = dummy;
        dummy.next = head;
        for (int size = 1; prev.next != null; size++) {
            int count = 0;
            LinkedLists.ListNode probe = prev.next;
            while (count < size && probe != null) { count++; probe = probe.next; }
            if (count % 2 == 0) {
                LinkedLists.ListNode groupHead = prev.next, cur = groupHead, rev = probe;
                for (int i = 0; i < count; i++) { LinkedLists.ListNode nx = cur.next; cur.next = rev; rev = cur; cur = nx; }
                prev.next = rev;
                prev = groupHead; // old head is now the group's tail
            } else {
                for (int i = 0; i < count; i++) prev = prev.next;
            }
        }
        return dummy.next;
    }

    // ---------- Insertion Sort List (LC 147): O(n^2) time, O(1) space, dummy head ----------
    static LinkedLists.ListNode insertionSortList(LinkedLists.ListNode head) {
        LinkedLists.ListNode dummy = new LinkedLists.ListNode(Integer.MIN_VALUE);
        while (head != null) {
            LinkedLists.ListNode nx = head.next, p = dummy;
            while (p.next != null && p.next.val < head.val) p = p.next;
            head.next = p.next;
            p.next = head;
            head = nx;
        }
        return dummy.next;
    }

    // ---------- Convert Binary Number in a Linked List to Integer (LC 1290) ----------
    static int getDecimalValue(LinkedLists.ListNode head) {
        int v = 0;
        for (LinkedLists.ListNode n = head; n != null; n = n.next) v = (v << 1) | n.val;
        return v;
    }

    // ---------- Remove Linked List Elements (LC 203) ----------
    static LinkedLists.ListNode removeElements(LinkedLists.ListNode head, int val) {
        LinkedLists.ListNode dummy = new LinkedLists.ListNode(0), tail = dummy;
        dummy.next = head;
        while (tail.next != null) { if (tail.next.val == val) tail.next = tail.next.next; else tail = tail.next; }
        return dummy.next;
    }

    // ---------- Insert into a Sorted Circular Linked List (LC 708) ----------
    static LinkedLists.ListNode insertCircular(LinkedLists.ListNode head, int x) {
        LinkedLists.ListNode node = new LinkedLists.ListNode(x);
        if (head == null) { node.next = node; return node; }
        LinkedLists.ListNode cur = head;
        while (true) {
            boolean between = cur.val <= x && x <= cur.next.val;
            boolean atWrap = cur.val > cur.next.val && (x >= cur.val || x <= cur.next.val); // cur is the max, cur.next the min
            if (between || atWrap || cur.next == head) { // cur.next == head: all equal values, any slot works
                node.next = cur.next;
                cur.next = node;
                return head;
            }
            cur = cur.next;
        }
    }

    // ---------- Cycle length and cycle entry together: Floyd phase 1 finds a meeting point, then count a lap ----------
    static int cycleLength(LinkedLists.ListNode head) {
        LinkedLists.ListNode slow = head, fast = head;
        while (fast != null && fast.next != null) {
            slow = slow.next;
            fast = fast.next.next;
            if (slow == fast) {
                int len = 1;
                for (LinkedLists.ListNode n = slow.next; n != slow; n = n.next) len++;
                return len;
            }
        }
        return 0;
    }

    // ---------- Flatten a Multilevel Doubly Linked List (LC 430): iterative with a stack of "next" pointers ----------
    static class DNode {
        int val;
        DNode prev, next, child;
        DNode(int v) { val = v; }
    }

    static DNode flatten(DNode head) {
        Deque<DNode> st = new ArrayDeque<>();
        DNode cur = head, last = null;
        while (cur != null) {
            if (cur.child != null) {
                if (cur.next != null) st.push(cur.next);
                cur.next = cur.child;
                cur.child.prev = cur;
                cur.child = null;
            }
            last = cur;
            if (cur.next == null && !st.isEmpty()) {
                cur.next = st.pop();
                cur.next.prev = cur;
            }
            cur = cur.next;
        }
        return head;
    }
}

Pitfalls

  1. Use a dummy head whenever the head can be removed or replaced.
  2. Circular list insert: handle all-equal values and the wrap point (max then min).
  3. After reversing a group, its old head becomes the tail: reconnect to the next group.

String Algorithms

KMP and the Z-function give linear pattern matching and expose periodic structure; Rabin-Karp hashes windows (use two moduli and verify); Manacher finds the longest palindrome in O(n). The rest are careful big-number and parsing routines.

PatternUse caseComplexity
KMPPattern search, repeated pattern, shortest palindromeO(n + m)
Z-functionAll occurrences, prefix matchesO(n + m)
Rabin-KarpRolling hash, duplicate substring with binary searchO(n) expected
ManacherLongest palindromic substringO(n)
